reviews.author: Chetan Motamarri
reviews.text:
Amazing Stay at Paradisus Cancún

Our stay at Paradisus Cancún was fantastic, with beautiful surroundings, great service, and a relaxing ambiance.

Dining – Vegetarian Options

The resort has 6-7 specialty restaurants requiring reservations and a buffet available for walk-ins. While vegetarian options were limited, Cielo stood out with its authentic Mexican flavors and local spices, they have some good options Vegetarian/Vegan.

A huge shoutout to Patricia and Moises from Cielo! They went above and beyond to make our son’s birthday truly special. Patricia’s warmth, attention to detail, and exceptional hospitality made us feel like VIP guests. Moises was equally wonderful, ensuring we had the best experience and food. Their dedication made our trip even more memorable!

Resort & Amenities: Beach Cabana & Pool are beautifully designed and perfect for relaxation. The lush greenery inside the hotel added a unique charm.

Activities – Could Be Better

Weekend activities were decent, but weekday options were lacking. More engaging evening entertainment would improve the experience.

Overall great luxury stay with excellent service, a relaxing atmosphere, and beautiful aesthetics. Patricia and Moises made a lasting impression, and we would definitely return!

reviews.author: Sebastian Ripoll
reviews.text:
I'm truly surprised that, given the price, many things aren't included in the "all-inclusive" package. What truly shocks me is that a chain with such a prestigious name offers a cot as a bed for an adult... and the response is that there's nothing to be done about it. One person slept terribly, and on a completely different note, they should have staff on the beach to ensure there are chairs available. It's unbelievable that we can't even go to the beach because of this.

The wine they offer is poor, and the only steakhouse is an extra charge. The services they offer free of charge are unacceptable for a 5-star hotel. It's more like a 3 or 4-star hotel compared to other chains I've stayed at with the same model. At the pool, where people usually gather at lunchtime, there were 20 people waiting during peak hours for just one (yes, only one) person serving. At 11 pm, all the bars close, so they stop serving drinks.

The hotel itself is beautiful. The lobby or main lounge is incredible, with its stunning greenhouse and natural surroundings, and the beach is divine. The water is choppy and rough, not really suitable for children, at least at this time of year.

Unfortunately, I have to return to a Meliá hotel in Punta Cana in a few days, and after this experience, I don't want to go back... Let's see if it's just Mexico or if the whole chain is like this.

reviews.author: Amanda Refearo
reviews.text:
March 2025

Our family trip was incredibly meaningful, marking multiple celebrations: my parents' 40th wedding anniversary, our 7th anniversary, and both my son's and my birthdays. It was extra special as our first family trip together ever.

Upon arrival, our excitement dwindled when we were assigned our rooms. Despite our requests, nothing was accommodated or acknowledged. Romina at the front desk informed us that nothing could be changed due to a big group arriving the next day, making us feel like we didn’t matter. Not to mention, there was nothing special setup in our rooms for our special occasions like we've experienced at other resorts.

Our initial rooms felt like a hole in the wall on the basement-like bottom floor—claustrophobic, and the balcony faced a wall. Displeased, I returned to the front desk. Thankfully, Enrique was helpful. He changed my parents’ room to a higher floor and provided us with a room with the king-size bed we prioritized, though still on the bottom floor.

Enrique promised room changes could occur in 3 days, as they would be available by the 15th. We accepted this and was asked to return in 20 mins for our room, only to encounter Romina again. She told us the earlier promise couldn’t be fulfilled due to the large group arriving the next day, displaying a very bad attitude unwilling to help and seeming intent to block Enrique's solution.To prevent further distress, I accepted the situation with the new room, which faced only half a wall this time, resolving to not let these issues ruin our hard-earned trip.

At first glance, the room seemed acceptable, but as we settled in, it became clear how worn out everything was. Two lights were out, making the room very dim. The bathroom was filthy and appeared improperly cleaned; the tub looked like it needed replacing. This was the worst cleanliness I've encountered at an all-inclusive. Over our 7-nights stay, the cleaning person showed up only 2 times, our fridge was never stocked, until we complained and even then it only got stocked on the last day. Midway through the trip, we discovered 2 mid-sized roaches in the room and later encountered many tiny baby roaches in the bathroom.

The food was below average. Despite a wide array of options, the dishes didn't taste great and were often overly salty.

During our stay the large group ended up being a corporate conference who were not being serviced privately resulting in huge lines everywhere and multiple nights of large private dinners by the main pool where the entertainment would typically be being blocked off and only accessible to the conference goers changing the atmosphere for people who are there on vacation.

The beach was the highlight, even during a windy week when the water was too rough to swim in. The service from Eduardo at the beach club with the Kanna Bali beds was excellent, though not included, costing an additional $250 USD or available as a gift if you endure a sales pitch for Club Melia membership. I strongly advise against joining Club Melia. The brand lacks integrity and consistently fails to address issues promptly, missing multiple opportunities to make things right. why join a club when they can't do things right the first time? Second or third..

Activities for kids were well-managed by Nestor, who ran the workshops admirably and beach activities. The kiddie pool section was great for young children, with knee-high water, though it wasn't cleaned daily and seating was limited.

The 9-hole golf course, was neglected, with broken bottles and very rough greens.

The main area in building 3 is dreamy with all the vines coming down, but that's where it ends.. everything else shows its age. The resort is closing in May for a year-long renovation, and it seems many staff have lost motivation or aren't performing at full potential during this time and it shows.

Would we return? No, because our business didn’t feel valued at all. I highly recommend saving your money, time, and energy by booking elsewhere.. somewhere where they actually care about your experience.

I honestly think giving two stars is being generous. I stayed for my bachelorette trip and was extremely disappointed.

3) we got back to our A/C leaking so bad it was flooding our room by the front door. We went down stairs to let the front desk know. Came back to it still leaking. reviews.author: malcyy
reviews.text:
10/10 Adults-Only Resort Experience

My girlfriend and I just got back from a week-long stay in the adults-only reserve area, and it was an incredible experience. We had a couple of minor issues during the first couple of days, but once we met Enrique, our concierge, everything changed for the better. Enrique went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect for us, from celebrating our anniversary with special in-room desserts, booking restaurant reservations to getting Bali beds—he really turned our trip into something special.

One of the highlights was the catamaran cruise, which we hadn’t done during our stay last year. The live jazz musician on the boat made it such a unique and fun experience, and we were thrilled it was included in the reserve package. Overall, the resort was just as peaceful and beautiful as we remembered, with clean beaches, amazing pools, and great food everywhere we went.

I also want to give a special shout-out to the incredible staff that made our trip unforgettable: Cynthia for pool activities and Spanish lessons, Oscar, Miguel and Victor for serving us at the pool, David for organizing our cabana, and Valeria, Javier, Josue, and Miguel at Sante Restaurant who made breakfast a highlight of our mornings.

From the friendly bellboys to the front desk staff, everyone at the resort made sure we had an amazing time. We’ll definitely be back again, and we can’t wait to see the same friendly faces after the renovations!

reviews.text: We stayed for 6 nights in the reserve section in March of this year. Everything was amazing. From as soon as we got to the resort the staff took our bags and had them delivered to our room, we got brought over to the Reserve check in, which was a super quick and simple process, and got welcome drinks from the staff and this all took maybe 15 minutes from start to finish. We were then advised that we would have a concierge throughout our trip and our concierge was amazing! We arrived around 8:30pm and weren’t expecting to hear from our concierge until the next day but we received a message from our amazing concierge Christian. Christian made our vacation so easy and relaxing and was honestly one of the best parts of staying at the resort. He went out of his way to reach out to us every morning and sent us a list of the daily activities and restaurant hours. He also met with us first thing the day after we arrived to book all of our a la carte reservations. He also offered to book excursions and spa appointments, Bali beds, and anything else we might have needed. He also booked us the sunset cruise that was included in our room which was amazing! Christian went out of his way to check in on us and say hello anytime he saw us around the resort. He always had a smile and was willing to go above and beyond. His amazing service made it even harder to leave the resort because it felt like we were leaving a friend behind. He even messaged us after we had checked out just to check in and make sure we had arrived at the airport safe and sound. We had also asked him in for a bottle of wine in our room and he gave us chocolate strawberries with it as well which was so nice. The resort itself was beautiful. The service at the pool Bali beds was amazing as well as at the Beach club beds. Jose, a server at the Capella restaurant was also amazing and so friendly! We really enjoyed all aspects of our trip and would love to come back. We also loved seeing Daisy the cat around the resort and loved that she was well taken care of by the resort and had her own bed. Thank you Paradisus staff for making our trip so wonderful and thank you so much Christian for all you did for us. Paradisus Cancun is very lucky to have someone as great as Christian working here.

Had a pretty amazing stay in January 2025. Really enjoyed it. My wife and I only stayed for two nights at the tail end of a 10 day tour of the Yucatan Peninsula. It was such a nice relaxing way to end our trip. If you aren't traveling with kids I would highly recommend upgrading to the reserve adults only package. No screaming kids, better drinks, nice outdoor restaurant overlooking the ocean private cabanas (is that what they're called??) by the pool. I'm not usually into fancy stuff and prefer a more authentic experience, like visiting Merida and Valladolid but I can't lie, spending two days at the Paradisus was awesome. I could never spend a week there, because I need to see some real stuff and meet people, try local food etc, but 2-3 days is so nice to just chill, have some nice
food and drinks and swim in the ocean. The beach there is beautiful. Swimming was fun but the waves may be too intense for some.
I would recommend Paradisus Cancún.

reviews.author: Ricky Yao
reviews.text: Amazing resort. The workers here are very welcoming and kind and can speak somewhat fluent English. All the food here is epic, especially Aqua Marine. Paradisus is more centered towards relaxation than activities. They have 2 huge pools, with one having a bar on it. This resort might not entertain younger kids too well, but there aren't too many things to do other than eat and relax on the beach or pool. Speaking of the beach, Paradisus has one of the longest stretches of beach area in the hotel zone. They have plenty of loungers at the beach and at the pools that come with umbrellas for shade. The rooms are packed with snacks and beverages, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, and they can be restocked daily. The overall tropical theme of Paradisus feels very relaxing and is the perfect escape from the depressing weather of my home.

reviews.author: Joti B
reviews.text:
Visited as a family with two children March 9-14th and had a great time! The hotel is only 15 minutes away from the airport making it a seamless commute.

PROS:

We booked through Expedia and were able to check-in a private lounge which made it comfortable and convenient. The resort overall is great for families with children and couples. There were many restaurants to choose from. I would recommend making the reservations the day you arrive to ensure you get your picks. The restaurants we really enjoyed included Lemon Fish  which was Sushi and Japanese inspired food and Capella which was Italian cuisine. This was the consensus we received from the reviews and guests visiting. The buffet was also pleasant. We preferred eating breakfast at the buffet and lunch at Masi’s Pizza which is poolside. Room service was also good. The amenities were top notch and providing many areas to lounge and enjoy time with your loved ones with a great view. Coffee is a must when I travel and the Nespresso bar did not disappoint! The beach was extremely clean and water was crystal blue. I also liked that there were not vendors trying to sell you services every other minute. The gym and tennis court are also great!

CONS:

As mentioned in previous reviews the rooms are outdated. They will be closed for 1 year in a few months and I’m assuming they will be updating the rooms. In addition, you have to wake up at 6 am to hold beach chairs and pool chairs for yourself and loved ones, as after 7 am they are not available. We encountered a rude waiter at Capella restaurant on March 10th at 9pm. Otherwise, service was great!

Overall, our group of 7 had a great time! I would recommend requesting a room in pyramid 4 if you are travelling with kids as this was a central location to everything!

reviews.author: Jessica Gerein
reviews.text:
We visited the Paradisus Cancun in March 2025, please note I believe they are renovating part of the resort in June 2025 - so there will likely be changes!

Pros:
- Food was amazing! We ate at the buffet, ordered poolside and visited many of the a La cartes - I can say hands down this is the best food I have had at an all inclusive! No one out of our group got sick
- Stroller/wheelchair friendly - ramps everywhere!
- Room Service - pretty good selection for 24hr room service. It did typically take 1hr on average. We got breakfast twice and it was delicious!
- Beach was AMAZING! White white sand and bluest water I have ever seen
- wrist band hotel keys for your room is always a bonus!
- staff were very helpful and friendly!
- very delicious drinks and large variety or drinks!

Cons:
- All Bars close by 11pm…. LIKE WHAT?!?! This was sad. The Ginger Bar turns into a club from 10pm-11pm which was fun! Wish it stayed open later
- not much seating near bars for the evening. They had a lot of ‘beds’ but we wished they had more tables or seating areas to sit and play cards but still be near the bar!
- not enough loungers by the pool. Had to wake early to get chairs
- chairs on balcony were often missing or broken
- they do not always stock your mini bar - I was breast feeding and had a baby who took some bottles, so bottled water was necessary and sometimes hard to get!

Information:
- Golf Course - 9 hole - Par 3 course: green fees are included with the all-inclusive package, but you do pay to rent clubs. This costed $25USD to rent, but they let us share clubs! The course is OK, and there are no golf carts or dress requirements
- Dinner Reservations: there was no limit on reservations! But you can only book 3 nights in advanced
- Resort Photographers - we booked a session and the photos turned out great, but it is pricy. It is $20USD/photo which you received digitally, or could do a package for a large quantity of photos and receive a photo book! We did the later option, and will cherish capturing these memories forever!
- travelling with Baby: crib is not guaranteed- but we received one! If there is not one available, you could probably get one the next day! They provide crib sheets & pillow. It is a wooden or plastic deep crib.
- Rooms: our room had a kitchenette. Having cupboards, a kitchen sink and hot plate was very helpful when travelling with a baby! I wish we knew this before we hauled down a pop-up sink and kettle! Some rooms have bath tubs, some rooms have walk-in showers. I am guessing some this may change for the Reno’s!

Overall, we really enjoyed the Paradisus Cancun and are intrigued to see the changes once the Reno is complete!

He not only took care of everything we needed as far as reservations, and answering any & all questions we had, but he went out of his way & went above & beyond for us. Malva buffet was impressive,  always a huge selection everyday.
Aqua marine we had a beautiful sea bass and mushroom risotto.  & My my husband really enjoyed our dinner at Sal steak house.  The staff by the reserve pool were great! Especially Oscar! I was getting a little too much sun one afternoon,  and he brought an umbrella over and kept adjusting it so I wouldn't be in the direct sun. Ceasar was great too!

reviews.author: Julia Blazejewski
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights in early March 2025. After reading many five star reviews prior to arriving, we were surprised to realize that our stay did not match other guests’ experiences.

The room we received was in definite need of an upgrade; the bathroom was pretty run down, and the couch in the room had stains on it. We were not expecting a fancy room by any means because we knew we booked the most basic option. However, we were still expecting the room to be in good condition. Also, when booking, I was told I would receive a $200 credit to be used for a room upgrade. When we arrived, we found out only $50 of the $200 could be used for a room upgrade, which was not nearly enough. I had called the resort a couple months prior to clarify the credit, and even then, no one had informed me of the full terms of the credit. This felt very misleading.

We didn’t have any issues getting reservations at the restaurants, but the food was not good and not up to par with what should be served at a four-star resort. The service was not that great either. Some of the servers came off as slightly rude, and nobody really checked up on us. At Lemon Fish, we waited almost an hour for our server to take our order and bring our meal out. We also did not appreciate that the servers occasionally tried to up charge us by trying to sell the food and drink upgrade options, but not telling us they would cost extra unless we explicitly asked. The food at the buffet was alright, and was honestly a better option for dinner than the restaurants. The dessert options were bad; the ice cream by the pool was delicious though and one of the highlights of the resort. The drinks were good, but watered down which is to be expected at an all inclusive. The best drinks were at Ginger bar.

The resort is beautiful, and the beach and pools are perfect. I recommend waking up at 7-8 am to claim seating by the pool or beach, as it fills up pretty quickly. The resort also had nightly entertainment, which was nice.

All in all, if food and service are important factors for you, I would recommend staying elsewhere. I imagine that booking at The Reserve could make it a little more worthwhile though.

reviews.author: Sydni Worley
reviews.text:
I am going to start by saying I have literally never written a review before. Usually if it is a positive experience, I unfortunately forget. If it is a bad experience, I try to just brush it off.

But months later, I am still thinking about how absolutely horrible our experience was at this resort. It was my husband and I’s honeymoon. When we first walked in, the experience was nothing short of magical. They offered us a drink right when we walked in, the resort was beautiful, and the customer service was great (other than the fact that we had to wait 45 minutes for them to check everyone who had just entered in, but we both had a drink in hand and were in such a dreamland, we didn’t mind!)

The first two days were great. My husband and I restaurant hopped, drank espresso martinis, and truly just had a blast. The lady in charge of entertainment was just amazing. My husband and I did water pilates, and it is still one of our favorite memories to this day!

Unfortunately, that is where the magic came to an end. We had excursions planned for our 4th and 5th day, and we were so excited. That is, until my husband woke up violently throwing up. I went to the front desk requesting a doctor, and they made light of the situation by asking if it was just alcohol poisoning. Listen, I get it. It is a private all-inclusive resort, they most likely have several customers who over indulge in beverages. This was simply not the case for us. It was clearly food poisoning. I went back to our room after this, praying he would start to feel better in the next few hours. But when 4pm rolled around, and he was still gagging (at this point blood), I decided we needed a doctor. The doctor came to our room after telling me that at minimum it would be a $500 charge, which was a huge number as a young newly wed couple, but we had to stomach it. The doctor did help, but I will say, at one point I saw him looking on safari to see if certain medicines could mix and he couldn’t really explain to me what he was giving my husband. He then told me that if he didn’t stop throwing up in the next hour, we would need to get a ride to the nearest emergency room which was an HOUR away. I felt completely alone, and considering he was suffering from food poisoning from THEIR food, I would have assumed they would cover most charges or at least offer to help us get a ride.

Thankfully, my husband took a turn for the better. He slept the rest of the evening, finally getting a break from throwing up. And I went to dinner by myself that night, which was just so sad on our honeymoon.

The next day, things got WORSE! My husband was feeling somewhat better, but could only stomach eating bread. At this point, I was nervous to touch any of the food so I did basically the same thing. We spent most of the day on the beach and when we came back in the room to get ready for dinner, I was going to put on my wedding ring. I had tried hiding it every other day, but this day, we were just so excited to be back outside that I completely forgot to hide it. While we were gone, some member of room service came in and stole my ring. We spent over an hour digging in the room, going through everything. In order to report a stolen item, we had to have police come into our room to also search through our items. They then told us that it would take 72 hours to conduct interviews and that it would be hard to know who did it considering around 20 people have access to our room at any point (this is kind of an unsettlingly large number of people in my opinion) and that it was most likely a lost cause. That was it. They didn’t offer to do anything. That was our last night there before waking up the next morning just so happy to finally get to leave.

This was actually all together a terrible experience and a nightmare of a honeymoon. My husband and I have talked about redoing our honeymoon experience at our one year. This time, however, it will be in the mountains.

reviews.author: Pri Sommelier
reviews.text: What can I say about Paradisus (extra charge for The Reserve category)? We arrived on Sunday and left Saturday morning. Even on Sunday, when we arrived, the receptionists didn't know where to send us to eat. We had to rely on our own intuition to find somewhere to eat, since beach bars and restaurants close at 4 pm. We managed to get cold cuts and cheeses at the cafeteria. It's worth noting that we weren't offered any drinks or anything at reception. Monday morning wasn't any better. For breakfast at Sante, we ordered scrambled eggs, which arrived without bread because they were out. They didn't know how to fix it. Two days later, at another breakfast, the bread arrived, and 50 minutes later, the eggs (very disappointing). The sun loungers without shade at the pools or beach designated for The Reserve guests (not exclusive at all) were available. We learned from the assigned concierge that you only have two days during your entire stay to use the shaded loungers (again, very exclusive). It's worth mentioning that alcohol stops at 11 PM throughout the hotel, and the minibar only has beer. If you order wine, it's the same for the entire hotel, costs $9, and you won't have access to it in your room. The hotel is geared towards Americans; they always speak to you in English and provide better service if you speak English. None of the service staff seem to know the hotel's operating hours. Please don't use room service; it takes an hour and a half to get a burger and wings, and when you ask for ice, it never arrives. The restaurants are decent. Capella is bad (overcooked pasta and sour sauce), Agua Marina is okay (they take your food away before you finish, which makes it bad), Sante is decent for dinner, Sal is good if you like American-style meat (charred on the outside but cooked to perfection), Malva is acceptable for a buffet and has some highlights, although it's always packed. Mascalzone is decent for stone-baked pizza (they don't have calzones or mushrooms). The lemon fish sushi was forgettable, but the octopus was outstanding. The Flora was delicious, with good use of ingredients and friendly service. I especially appreciated the service from the gentleman at the Nespresso café in The Reserve area! In short, a beautifully decorated hotel with sublime architecture, terribly managed and forgettable for the price.

reviews.author: Chad Bacon
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed at Paradisus Cancun from 2/8-2/14. Overall, we were disappointed with our stay. This is not a 5 star hotel and the poor quality of the rooms, food and drinks reflects that. Don't be fooled.

The biggest thing that turned us off to the Paradisus was the "concierge" staff that are actually part of the sales staff for the Melia Circle Club. Upon arrival, we were approached by Oscar, a concierge. Looking back, his friendly conversation was used to gather info on us to see if we could to suckered into buying a membership into the Melia Circle Club. Oscar told us to find him later for our free welcome gift for simply staying at the hotel. The next day, Oscar asked us if we wanted our gift, which was going to be a new beach bag, a massage for my wife and a discounted massage for myself. He sat us down by the sales office and over more friendly banter he told us that to receive free gifts we had to go through a presentation, that would take 30-45 minutes. We declined, but Oscar said that we would be helping him, as he receives a bonus for each group that goes through the presentation. His exact words were "just play the game." We accepted, as we still thought he was a good guy who truly cared about us as guests. During this time, he also promised me a bottle of tequila to take home. Once we accepted, he brought over another "concierge" named Cinthia, whom he said was his boss and he just wanted to show her he was doing his job. Cinthia then brought over the "big boss" an older, gentleman, who led us into the sales room and introduced us to a salesperson, Eduardo.

The presentation began with questions on how much we paid to stay at the hotel, how often we travel, how often we would like to travel, etc. He recommended we join the blue membership, which is entry level. For the LOW PRICE of $36,255, we could join, which would allow us access to low rates to other Melia properties, upgraded rooms/food/drink for free, etc. We would need to ONLY put $12,000+ down today and pay a LOW monthly payment of $869/month at 8% interest for 36 months, which came out to ONLY $1255/month with 4 weeks at hotels for free. I couldn't help but laugh at this offer. Eventually the offer became $29,000, with $2500 down and $369/month BEFORE interest with 7 weeks free. He said to keep this deal quiet because it was so good. Ha! I continued to say no, even though Eduardo said that type of money is nothing for Americans and that he recently sold a Canadien couple who were younger than us and the husband was "just the manager of a store." The back and forth continued and he offered to take less money down, $499 and finance for 48 months. I informed him there was no way we were going to say yes despite his trips to the office of the "big boss" to get a "better deal." Eduardo ended the presentation asking me if I want to pay double or triple to travel and I told him, yes, that is fine with me. Before leaving he asked one final time if he made the monthly payment lower to $200/month or $100/month, would we sign. No Eduardo, we want to leave. After an hour, we were finally out of there without joining the club.

After that, Oscar was no where to be found and over the next few days. If we saw him he would bury his head in his phone or pretend like he didn't see us. Suspicious, I did some research on the Melia Circle Club and if you look online, it is described as a scam by those who unfortunately signed the contract. On our last night, we ran into Oscar and he asked where we had been, to which my wife responded, where have you been and where is my free massage? He acted shocked that we hadn't received the gifts promised and blamed Eduardo. We had already gone to the spa for massages so I declined his offer for a massage coupon. He then offered me $100 at the hotel gift shop which I laughed at. We settled on a $100 gift certificate, as we had extra charges from dinnerss. I brought up the bottle of tequila he had promised and he said he would get it to me that day. I never received a bottle of tequila. BEWARE OF THESE PREDATORY PRACTICES!

reviews.author: Javier Sanchez
reviews.text: Paradisus advertises itself as a 5-star all-inclusive hotel, which is completely false. In reality, it has many things to improve before it can truly be called that. Today is March 4, 2025, and we just returned from a 3-night stay. From the very first day, I wanted to leave. I've stayed at several resorts in Mexico, and this one has been the most boring, exploitative, and with terrible service from the staff. I found it very strange that the employees were so rude and provided such poor service, but it's the hotel's fault because they are understaffed, especially in the beach area. In every other resort I've been to, except this one, there's a beach bar and snack area where you can go and order whatever you want or serve yourself, but not here. Since we had to order from a single waiter who was serving everyone on the beach, and you order something and it takes forever to get it... so we decided to go up and order and get our own drinks and snacks, but they wouldn't give us anything because, according to our waiter, he had to bring it to us. So our time at the beach was terrible. Another thing I didn't like is that they don't have any entertainment except the shows, which, by the way, they give you a QR code to check schedules and locations, and then you go and find out that the entire program and locations are different; and the three days we were there, they scheduled the international restaurants at the times the shows started, and we either went to the show or the restaurants, which was awful! The shows are the only free entertainment they have! Since they don't have anything else! That's why we were super bored, and there was an area called Escape, I think it was, and we went there so my daughter would be entertained. It turns out it cost money... super expensive, $800 per person! I mean, they charge for everything: a sunbed, room service, games, and I was even afraid to ask the waiters anything because they always want tips for everything. If you don't have cash in hand, nobody moves. Don't operate like an all-inclusive resort! Don't scam tourists! I saw all the foreigners there struggling just like us, and besides, they didn't have enough sunbeds; they were all strewn on the sand because there wasn't enough space. And the spaces they did have cost $250 each—it's a total rip-off! There was no entertainment on the beach, no music; that was only in the areas where you pay $250 for your sunbed. We found a cockroach in our room, the food in the restaurants was terrible in both taste and variety, and only one restaurant was open; you had to make a reservation for all the others. Suddenly, in any area of ​​the hotel you walked around—tables, chairs, etc.—they told you it was reserved because someone had already paid. Honestly, I've been to much cheaper resorts with top-notch service; this hotel was nothing like it. The only thing we liked was the beach water, and that was only because it wasn't theirs. I feel bad for all the other foreigners I saw because they were treated the same way; they must have been very disappointed.

I stayed in February 2025.

I arrived by car and Raúl very kindly greeted us and was always very friendly.

A young woman (I apologize, I didn't write down her name) kindly took us to check in at The Reserve; she was very friendly and courteous.

Check-in was a bit of a hassle, an area for improvement.

I had requested a dinner reservation before my arrival, but unfortunately, it wasn't made, which was a bit frustrating. Fortunately, we were welcomed without a reservation at Blue Agave, and I want to congratulate Atilano, who took wonderful care of us and had a very positive attitude that lifted my spirits that night. Thank you so much.

I also want to thank the butler, who was always helpful via WhatsApp, even though I never met him in person. He was very attentive.

Dinner at Sal Steak Cave was delicious, and Leo kindly made me a clericot even though it wasn't on the menu. The food was also delicious.

Jesús at Limón Fish also recommended a tropical drink with mezcal—yum, delicious!

I had a treatment at the spa, and everything was great, but what I liked most was the hydrotherapy circuit. Thanks, Ismael, for the attention.

At the pool, I never lacked anything thanks to Yamil, who was always attentive.

And of course, Mr. Guillermo at Malva was always very active during the hotel's peak hours, but very helpful and friendly at all times. Congratulations!

The room was fine but needs updating; I think they'll be renovating soon. The minibar in the room wasn't cooling, but since the Atrium at The Reserve has everything and is so convenient, it wasn't necessary.
The gym was good; the equipment was well-maintained. The hotel doesn't offer turndown service. However, the room had a spectacular view. A very positive experience, highly recommended.

reviews.author: Alexandre Contreras
reviews.text:
Non-Reserve, with 2 kids (8 and 10)

HOTEL - Beautiful and clean. The main pyramid is simply stunning at night. The complex is big and you can get lost at first while navigating the pyramids, but you'll find your way eventually.

ROOM - I have a basic room in Pyramid 4. It's definitely outdated. The room is on the side of the pyramid, so my view is the other pyramid, which sucks a bit, but you can stil see the ocean. While outdated, the room is fine, nothing to complain.

POOL - The non-Reserve pool is huge, but the bar, DJ and activities are specifically on one end of the pool. It's very nice and clean. Beautiful view as well. Available chairs are hard to find.

BEACH - Very nice beach, beautiful water. Right next to the resort, literally a 30 seconds walk from the pool. Again, chairs are hard to find.

RESTAURANTS - The food at restaurants is very good, the buffet is great as well (definitely not out of this world, but very decent). However, the fact that you have to line up every day to make a reservation for restaurants is incredibly archaic, and I don't understand why guests can't make their reservations online. Lining up every day for 20 minutes to make a reservation is "not very 2025".

ROOM SERVICE - Somewhat varied and large menu for room service. We tried breakfast, and was amazing. It was quick, hot and well presented. I believe you have 3 free calls, then it's 6 USD.

ENTERTAINMENT - Pretty much inexistant.

GYM - Old equipment, but has pretty much everything you need for a decent workout. Pretty large and spacious as well.

KIDS ACTIVITIES - There is a Kidsdom, but it seems to be tailored for younger children. Basically you leave your kids there for a period of time, and you pick them up later. It would feel like punishment if I did that to a 8 and 10 year old. Otherwise, there is nothing really specific for kids.

STAFF - All of them have been super friendly, nothing to complain.

reviews.author: Mike Erikson
reviews.text:
NOT an ALL Inclusive - but a SOME Inclusive.  Upgrades anyone?  Lots of Lies, dirty facility, and my personal data was stolen from them!!!
As an international businessman I've traveled millions of miles and stayed at literally hundreds of hotels and this was my worst experience.  We were sold on upgrades and given documented promises (see screenshots) about what we would received and none of it came to fruition other than allowing us to eat at their "steak house" Sal which was terrible.  The included steak was a tiny (maybe 6 oz) sirloin (likely other meat - see pic) that was so chewy.  But when we arrived they rolled out a cart with a tomahawk, ribeye, fillet, waygu, and other lovely cuts.  NONE were included and cost up to $80 each!  Melia sold us on the NITKA which we upgraded to.  My nephew had an even nicer room and didn't pay for the upgrade, we didn't get a private check in, the Mayan blessing or the cruise.  Instead they offered to have a shanty van pick us up and take us to the cenote - NOT the same.  LOTS of bait and switch.  To my many followers - you'll see that most of my reviews are positive, obviously this one is not.

Plus THE BARS CLOSE EARLY!  I believe the pool bar closed at 4pm and all the rest at 9:pm.  This is the earliest of all the resorts I've stayed at.  I had tried to write this review last year but had too much to document and didn't get around to it.  It wasn't until this week when I was contacted by a solicitor that had ALL my travel details (flight, dates, room, quantity of people I traveled with, phone #, email, and more).  I asked Melia if they were with the company and it ends up they weren't.  Meaning MELIA had a data breach of my personal information!  The pool had debris in it, the glass railing had not been cleaned in months (covered in bird poo - see pictures), there was mold in the shower, my slider door would not close (in the NITKA upgrade room see pictures) and the breeze blowing across it was 81db (the volume of a coffee grinder - try sleeping with that) - you can see the daylight in the picture of my room, the light was broken and blinked at night, the safe was broken and beeped all night (they didn't have parts to fix it - see video) they wouldn't put us in another room (even though they had promised us a reserve room (see screenshot), the AC was broken and we spent over 3 hours on 3 separate occasions to wait for maintenance (see video),   There are MUCH better hotels that deliver on their promises and do not bait and switch and do not lose your personal data.  STAY ELSEWHERE!  As you can see I had it in writing - they still didn't honor it.  The only positive thing was it was a lovely location.  You can get this at another resort.  See the other recent ratings and choose wisely.  We had over 20 people the first week of May 2024 and had a wedding here and still got this treatment.

Scroll through the reviews and you will find many others.  IF you choose to ignore these - at least RECORD EVERY conversation you have as they will verbally promise even more and not stand behind that even.  Not that it matters because they will just apologize and act like they cannot do anything.  VERY corrupt hotel, and staff.  I worked at a resort in my teens and 20's and can honestly say they violate almost every good customer service standard.

reviews.author: Tania G
reviews.text:
Edit: I added a star for location and added another star because on our last couple of days, the food got better in the buffet and the pool was less crowded but still completely full.

Honestly one of the worst all inclusive hotels we have ever been to! I do not recommend this hotel. The hotel is managed very poorly and is extremely overbooked and understaffed. You will spend 90% of your time waiting in line! There is a line up for everything including the buffet breakfast. If you want to secure a bed besides the beach or the pool, you have to wake up at 4 am and put a towel on the chair to take it. Even that is not guaranteed as other guests might move your towel. You have to have your breakfast by 7 AM if you want to avoid a line up. During your stay, you will see many FIGHTS over chairs! Also, you will hear EVERYONE talk about having to wake up early to secure their spot because there are not enough chairs. The hotel will try to sell you a “cabana” experience for $250 USD/day and will tell you guests are not allowed to put their towel on chairs and encourage you to move their towels. Do not do this, the HOTEL is responsible to ensure you have a good experience so do not get involved with other poor guests trying to get a spot! The reality is the hotel just want you buy the cabana and will not provide enough chairs for their guests.
Activities are scheduled but do not follow the scheduled times and begin 20-30 minutes late. There is spinning on the schedule but out of the 4 days we showed up to the gym, none had an instructor.
Shows are average and performed near the pool. There is no stage and guess what? YEP, no CHAIRS.  There are not enough seats. 60% of people have to stand up and watch the show.
Although the Food stands and restaurants during the day have operating hours, they randomly close 20-30 minutes before the schedule. Even if you are in the line, they won’t serve you and will tell you it is closed.
Don’t waste your hard earned money. Food is average to good here and you will hear many reviews focused on food. But you won’t be able to relax here, there is too much tension. The only upside is staff are nice and the beach is beautiful, if you don’t mind having no shade or chair!
Also, there is a shortage of towels and restocking is not consistent. Although housekeeping is very nice, they don’t have enough towels to give you.
You won’t be able to get bottled water near the pool or the beach and they don’t restock it in your room frequently. They look you in the eye and tell you bottled water is for “reserved” guests ONLY. There is no kettle in the room to boil water.
There is also a line up for elevators and although we personally did not mind taking the stairs, if you are on the upper floors (7 or 8 ) consider that as a warning. You have to line up and wait 10-15 min for elevators.
Another weird thing is food is not seasoned well and there is no salt and pepper on tables.

I will never stay at this hotel again.

reviews.author: LuLu Jackson
reviews.text:
I just returned from my second stay at Paradisus Cancun – The Reserve, and I can confidently say it was even better than the first! From the moment we arrived, the service was absolutely exceptional. Every single staff member was warm, friendly, and truly made us feel like VIPs.

The biggest shout-out goes to Josué (Josh), our amazing waiter at the Balinese bed. He went above and beyond to make sure we had everything we needed, always with a smile. What really impressed us was his attention to detail: he remembered our names from one day to the next and made sure we were always comfortable. His service was, without a doubt, the best we've ever received at any resort!

Another team member who made our experience even more special was Miguel, one of our waiters, who was incredibly attentive and always remembered our drink orders, making sure we had exactly what we wanted without us even having to ask.

We also want to give a shout-out to Luis, our waiter at the cabana, who took wonderful care of us. She was always looking out for us, constantly checking if we needed anything and making sure our drinks were never empty. Her kindness and dedication truly made all the difference.

Our concierge, Rossana, was also amazing. She was so friendly and always ready to help us with anything we needed, ensuring our stay was perfect and worry-free. She truly elevated our experience and made us feel so well taken care of.

The resort remains as stunning as ever, but what truly made this trip unforgettable was the exceptional service from the incredible team. If you're looking for a luxurious, stress-free getaway with the most attentive staff, The Reserve at Paradisus Cancun is the place to be. We will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Mariana Gianelli
reviews.text: This is the third time I've visited the hotel. The last two times were excellent, which is why I decided to return. This time was truly disappointing. I suppose it has to do with the fact that it's closing for renovations in June of this year and reopening in 2026, so they don't seem to care if we're not happy. The hotel was packed. If you want to get a lounge chair, you have to get up at least at 6 am because after that, you have no choice but to lie down wherever there's space. When we arrived, the room was a disaster. There weren't enough lights, the air conditioning turned on and off randomly, and the step to the bathroom was broken. I asked for a room change, but they wouldn't give me one. They told me they were fully booked. Mind you, I had paid for it in August 2024, not at the last minute. The hotel staff is all very friendly; in fact, they're the ones keeping this hotel afloat. The food is impeccable, although if you go for dinner at 9 pm, you have to hope there's anything left because by 7 pm they've already eaten everything. I think they weren't prepared for so many people. I was completely disappointed with the hotel this time; next time I'll choose one where they don't have to apologize every 5 minutes.

reviews.author: Shaine Kumar
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Paradisus in Cancun for five days (February 1–6, 2025) with my girlfriend, family, and friends.

Positives: The beach is a highlight—spacious and enjoyable. The swim-up bar bartender was attentive and friendly, adding to the relaxed vibe. The buffet restaurant stood out as well, offering good food quality and a decent selection compared to other dining options.

Negatives: We paid for a Family Concierge Ocean View room, but upon arrival, we were assigned a bottom-floor room in Pyramid 3 with no view of the water at all. Despite complaining to the front desk, we received no resolution or assistance.

The restaurants, aside from the steakhouse, were disappointing. Service was consistently slow, and the food quality was subpar. I wouldn’t recommend booking most of the à la carte restaurants; I’d have preferred sticking to the buffet every night.

To make matters worse, on the second-to-last night, $100 CAD was stolen from our room—presumably by housekeeping. The money was in my girlfriend’s wallet, zipped inside another bag within a backpack. While it was our fault for not using the room safe, the incident was incredibly disappointing. We reported it to hotel security and staff, who promised to follow up after their investigation, but we never heard back—complete radio silence.

I won’t be returning to this property on my next visit to Cancun and will take my business elsewhere.

reviews.author: Vanessa
reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of staying at Paradisus Cancun for a week, and I cannot rave enough about the exceptional service and the unforgettable experiences we had during our stay. From the moment we arrived, the staff made us feel like royalty, and there are a few individuals who truly went above and beyond to make our trip unforgettable.

Alejandro and Ricardo at the coffee bar were incredible. They always greeted us with warm smiles, made our mornings a delight, and crafted the most delicious coffees. Their friendly demeanor and attention to detail really made each coffee break a special part of our day. Their dedication to customer service didn’t go unnoticed, and it was a pleasure starting each day with their wonderful drinks and service.

Guadencio at the beach was another standout. His hospitality was top-notch as he made sure we were always comfortable, providing us with refreshing drinks and ensuring we had everything we needed while soaking up the sun. He truly went out of his way to make our beach experience enjoyable and stress-free.

However, the one person who truly brightened our days was Francisco at the beach. From the very first interaction, he made us feel so welcome and valued. His upbeat attitude, genuine kindness, and outstanding service were unmatched. Francisco went above and beyond to ensure that we had the best possible experience, and he always made us smile with his thoughtful gestures and attentive care. He turned our beach days into something truly special, and I honestly can't thank him enough for his exceptional service.

The Paradisus Cancun resort exceeded all expectations, and I can’t wait to return. A huge thank you to Alejandro, Ricardo, Guadencio, and especially Francisco for making this trip one for the books. They each added a personal touch that truly elevated our experience. I highly recommend this resort to anyone looking for a luxurious, relaxing, and memorable vacation!

reviews.text:
We had a wonderful stay at Paradisius Cancun. The rooms were comfortable, the staff was friendly, and the food was delicious. I would especially like to thank Armando C. from the Malua Team AM at the buffet for making our mornings extra special. We had a large group (16) to accommodate, and Armando was always eager to help us and ensure we were well taken care of. Thank you, Armando! Our favorite restaurant was Lemon Fish, where our kids enjoyed an abundance of sushi. Jorge, our waiter, did a fabulous job.

The pool areas were clean and comfortable. Our only complaint was that we had to coordinate with our group to wake up around 5 AM to reserve seats at the pool. This was unexpected, considering we were on vacation!

Many other amenities were appreciated: freely available ice cream, coffee, and pastries. The popsicles at the lobby reception were a small but delightful addition. And the beach was enjoyable when the waves weren’t too rough. My brother and his family enjoyed a really cool snorkeling excursion just across the street. We were able to sneak out to the nearby shops too, just a short taxi ride away.

Thanks for an enjoyable holiday!

reviews.author: Dan Yockey
reviews.text:
One word: Horrible.

Checked in around 7pm, there was a line out the door. No sense of urgency by the front desk checking people in, the were processing one family about every 10-15 minutes, only two people working. That was my first introduction to the notion that everything at the hotel, and I mean everything, prepare to wait in line for  5-10 minutes minimum. That includes getting a coffee at the coffee bar, a drink at the pool bar, waiting in bread lines at the buffet and food stations, etc.  They simply can not or are unwilling to handle the proper throughput of a crowded resort.

The resort itself looks nice, but that's about all it has going for it. The pools have limited seating and chairs, so better get up at sunrise to reserve your spot.

The absolute worst part about this hotel is the dining. The servers come by about once to fill your glass. We tipped nicely the first couple days which had no affect on the service. I asked for a coffee in the morning one day and it never even showed up after asking three times. There was one server working the entire outdoor dining area. The buffet has limited food options, unappetizing, and unsanitary. Many plates sat there all night untouched because it looked like pig slop. Food was always lukewarm which is a major red flag for harboring foodborne bacteria. One night, a sewer line broke in the dining area and the staff were mopping it up and squeeging it away into a corner. The smell was unbearable, so we ate at a nearby restaurant. Absolutely appalling they even kept the dining room open, what a serious hazard to food safety. After witnessing that, to little surprise, our second to last day my entire family contracted a norovirus. All four of us vomited the entire last night we were there as well as all day the next day during the flight home. We asked housekeeping at midnight for fresh sheets, towels, and cleanup materials and it took over an hour for them to deliver. I went down to the front desk to getting to the bottom of the delay and they could not have shown any less concern about my sick family. It's not like they were even busy, the hallways were empty.

They obviously have bot accounts posting 5 star reviews. If you look closely most of the reviewers are new accounts with only one or two reviews, and they post little substance. This happens multiple times per day. It's pretty clear if you sort out the 1 star reviews that are being buried, they are all right on the mark with our experience.

Along with the 3+ hour wait in customs on arrival, my family and I are done with Cancun for a while.

•Waitress left while I was talking to her, never took dessert orders and ignored us until we just left.

reviews.author: J
reviews.text:
We just got back from Paradisus Cancún, me and my bf loved our stay! We paid extra to stay on the adult only section, our money was well spent.

-Check in
The check in process was seamless. A staff walked us to the adult only section to check in while the bell boy took care of our luggage. We were assigned a concierge, honestly it’s the best thing ever. Our concierge was great! She arranged /booked dinner reservations, tennis court, Bali bed etc for us so all we did was to tell her what we want to do and she took care of the rest.

- Room
Room was clean and well equipped with mini bar, Nespresso machine, safe etc. I was surprised to see the resort provided us with bug spray, sunscreen and slippers. No bad odour in the room.

- Food
Overall the food was great, with quite a lot of options on the resort. We loved the Mexican seafood restaurant Agua Marina! My bf love Flora as well. They have good room service as well, the ordering process was easy, we just called and scan the QR code for menu. Food came pretty timely after we called for room service. They also have some nice caffeinated drinks at the cafe.

- Staff
The staff are friendly and helpful. They speak pretty good English so no communication issue.

- Beach
The beach is beautiful with turquoise colour water and white sand! It was pretty well maintained with small amount of seaweed which I didn’t mind. Depending on the day, the wave could be quite strong.

- Pool
The adult only pool is nice and big, and well maintained. It wasn’t as crowded compared to the rest of the resort. Though most of the activities happened at the main pool in another section.

- Wild life
We came across a couple lizards on the resort and a sweet, lovely cat Daisy in her adult only section as well. My bf and I enjoyed watching wild animals so to us it wasn’t an issue.

- Check out
Check out day was super easy. Our concierge arranged the bell boy to come pick up our luggage. Our check out time was 12pm but our flight was at 8:30pm. The resort accommodated us and let us use the facilities on the resort until our pickup time. Our concierge booked us the hospitality room so we could shower prior to departure.

Overall we had a great time here and would definitely come back to Paradisus in the future!

reviews.author: Felipe Zafani
reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Incredible Stay at Paradisus Cancun – Amazing Service from Francisco!

Our stay at Paradisus Cancun was nothing short of amazing! From the breathtaking ocean views to the luxurious amenities, everything exceeded our expectations. But what truly made our trip special was the outstanding service we received—especially from Francisco, the beach server.

Francisco went above and beyond every single day to ensure we had everything we needed while relaxing by the beach. He was attentive, friendly, and always had a warm smile. Whether it was keeping our drinks refreshed, recommending the best cocktails, or simply making sure we were comfortable, his service was impeccable. His attention to detail and genuine hospitality made our beach days truly unforgettable!

If you’re staying at Paradisus Cancun, I highly recommend spending time on the beach and looking out for Francisco—he will make your experience even more enjoyable. We can’t wait to return to this beautiful resort and hope to see him again!

Thank you, Francisco, and the entire Paradisus Cancun team for an unforgettable vacation!

—Felipe Zafani

Just came back from my trip there.
Pros : Nice beach, the hotel public spaces are beautifull, staff members are very friendly and food is always available and you can always find something to eat.
Many mant activités for kids. Okay rooms, good A/C.

Cons : You will never be allowed to swim in the ocean at the resort. On a day with little to no wind flag was still red and lifeguard running after you if you go into the water. You can always go swim to neighbor resorts who were yellow most of the time.
There is not enough chairs at the pool/beach and people are fighting over it. Not sure if its on purpose, but you can rent a cabana for 250$ USD per day if you want to make sure to lay down somewhere other than the ground.
So many things at the other are only available to their elite members (somewhere to lay down at the pool, some restaurants, many meal choices at the restaurants, etc.)
We made sure when we booked to call the resort and ask if it was possible to get adjacent rooms since we were travelling with a baby and parents to make it easier. When we got there they told us it wasnt possible to put us on the same floor.

reviews.author: Nafia Khan
reviews.text: We had an amazing stay at paradisus cancun!! Veronica, manager relations of Meliá, made our stay special and memorable. She fixed any issues she had, was sympathetic, personable and extremely kind! We had the best time doing a couples massage and hydrotherapy at the spa. Boris is the manager at Lemon fish (Japanese fusion restaurant) and he also made our experience one of a kind with the service he gave us. He was just like a friend to us, always helped us out with reservations and introduced us to the head chef who is incredible there. The decor of this restaurant is stunning and so too is the food. We had the most phenomenal dessert there made specially that evening and we really have to thank Boris for his fantastic personality, we really hope to meet him again!! Fanny at the Flora restaurant is extremely kind and warm, she also helped us out with reservations here at this healthy restaurant. We loved the food and decor at flora - the tomato soup and salmon were excellent and the environment is truly enchanting. The Nespresso bar was another favourite of ours, we visited this as many times a day as we could because the coffee is incredible here and the service is extremely fast and nice. There is a reason the queue is always so long for the Nespresso bar (since it’s so delicious including all the fresh desserts they have - we are not even dessert people but we could not resist), and yet you’re never left waiting very long at all! The pools are so much fun here  and if you can get a Bali bed (we had one with a view of the beach), you will have the most relaxing and comfortable day. Even sitting on the beach chairs was wonderful - no seaweed in the water but the sea was rough! You have to go early in the day to get seats. The aquamarina restaurant is by the pool and it has the best shrimp tacos, nice dinner options too. The pizza bar and ice cream bar are also wonderful as pool-side snacks. We also loved the pool-side bar for fresh lemonade and mojitos! We had one bad waiter at the blue agave restaurant near Malva as he was quite rude but then all the other waiters and chefs were wonderful at breakfast and dinner. Malva is the buffet restaurant and the food is sub-standard (breakfast, lunch, dinner) but it is reliable. I would recommend you to try the restaurants when you can because the food is almost always better. We also had a bad experience with one waiter at Capella as we were sat at our table late (we had to wait a while) and then nobody came to take our order or serve us water for half an hour afterwards. The food was pretty good but it did take a while to come. The gym is also really nice here - most of the time we went (in the evening) it was empty, clean and well-equipped. Overall, this resort is lively and beautiful. Highly recommend this resort for the most memorable, magical stay!!!

reviews.author: Emir Exploring
reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

If you’re looking for a peaceful, luxurious getaway—this is NOT the place for you. Paradisus Cancun markets itself as a high-end, all-inclusive resort, but in reality, it feels more like an overpriced, overcrowded party hotel with subpar service and mediocre food.

First off, the food quality is nowhere near what you’d expect from a “luxury” resort. Bland, uninspired, and barely edible at times. The buffets feel like a glorified cafeteria, and the VIP restaurants? Good luck getting a reservation unless you enjoy eating at 10 PM.

Want to relax in the evening? Too bad. There’s a DJ blasting music until midnight every single night. Apparently, the resort thinks we all came here for a Vegas-style nightclub experience rather than a tranquil beachside retreat. Forget about getting a peaceful night’s sleep—you’ll be serenaded by bass thumping through the walls instead.

And let’s talk about customer service. Or rather, the complete lack of it. Staff are indifferent at best and dismissive at worst. Any issue you bring up is met with either confusion or a vague “we’ll look into it,” which, spoiler alert, never happens. It’s almost impressive how little they care.

For the price we paid, I expected a luxurious, relaxing experience. Instead, I got loud music, disappointing food, and indifferent service. I truly don’t feel like I’m on a vacation at a luxury resort. If you’re considering booking here, do yourself a favor and look elsewhere.

reviews.text:
Rooms are dated in the first pyramid. We had to complain due to mold and the degradation of the room, for example the fan was swinging off the ceiling as many mounts were off the roof and the towel rack was not screwed into the wall. Pyramid 1 was also the farthest away and took 10-15min walk with our baby.

They addressed our concerns by moving us into pyramid 3 and it was much better. The room was updated and the convenience of its location was central to the whole resort including all the restaurants. It was a much desired change.

Service has been great. We were disappointed at first being left without service at one of the restaurants but the next night, Armando at Blue Agave turned out whole mood around. He was very helpful, very entertaining, and his service was excellent.

The restaurants are much better than the buffet. Reservation based.

Location is good with the beach. Convenient from the airport with the shuttle. Only 20 minutes. It is definitely one of those places where you have to get up in the morning to occupy spaces for the pool and the beach.

The rooms need to be updated but the staff here are very accommodating to your concerns and in the end, know how to make things right.

EDIT: I would also like to highlight that Rommel with guest services and Ignacio at Sal Steak House helped to provide an exceptional customer service experience for myself and my family. Thank you to you both for creating exceptional experiences.

reviews.author: Rosa Matheus
reviews.text:
This is not a 5-star hotel. I recommend you consider other hotel options at the same price before booking here.

I'm sharing several experiences we had in just one day at this hotel. We arrived yesterday, February 19th, and immediately had some bad experiences.

1- We booked a shuttle service from the hotel, but they made us wait at least 40 minutes to leave from the airport.
2- The rooms are quite far apart, so if you want to request something for your room, like a dental kit or a hairdryer (which wasn't in our room), you have to wait about 30 minutes for it to be delivered.

3- You have to make reservations in advance during the day to book the restaurants where you want to have dinner. 4- There's an ENDLESS line at the buffet for breakfast between 8:30 am and 10:30 am.
5- The buffet area is tiny, the number of people there makes it impossible to have a pleasant breakfast, and the lines inside the buffet for eggs or omelets are EXTREMELY LONG.
6- We ordered coffee for breakfast, and it arrived just as we were leaving.

7- The bars have limited alcohol; you can't get 12-year-old whiskey, and it costs extra. Drinks like coconut water also cost extra (10 USD).

8- During the day, it's impossible to get a lounge chair; they are extremely limited and completely occupied by 8 am. By 9 am, none are available.

9- Finally, at check-in, they don't take into account the preferences specified during the reservation. They tried to change the double bed selected by a couple of friends to single beds. 9- There are no lounge chairs available on the beach either, and the sunbeds for relaxing cost $250 USD to rent per day.

Finally, a group of eight of us came to this hotel, paid around $500 USD per night, and it's not worth it. DO NOT COME TO THIS HOTEL. Choose options like Xcaret or the Hyatt for a similar price and a much better experience, without a doubt.

I hope this helps :)

reviews.text:
We had an overall great stay at Paradisus Cancun. We stayed in the adults only reserve section and made sure to take full advantage of the all inclusive benefits. We ate so much food and enjoyed poolside service with a drink in our hands at almost all times, mainly thanks to Yamil and Oscar.

Our concierge, Enrique, was attentive, accommodating, and always available. He did his very best to get the reservations at the restaurants and times we requested and sent us our daily activities each morning. He also booked us a poolside cabana for our last two days and made sure to get us the sunset cruise on Saturday.

Three issues we ran into:

1. Our original room was incorrect. They had my wife and I in a room with a double bed that was not an ocean view. Nevertheless, they made up for it by switching our room the next morning that matched our intended reservation.

2. When we arrived to the hotel, we were fortunate that Enrique had booked dinner reservations for us but a lot of days and times were already booked. I am not sure how this happens when booking the restaurants ourselves prior to arrival is not an option.

3.  Our pickup at the airport was not readily available which meant we had to wait for about an hour to get a ride to the hotel, through their transportation provider, Otium.

Still yet, the people, the service from the staff, and the hotel itself made it a very nice stay. We would definitely come back to Paradisus in the future.

Jorge at Blue Agave was an exceptional server who took the time to guide us through the extensive menu. I wish the hotel had a system where if a chair was left alone for more than 30 minutes, it would be given to the next guest waiting. We saw many chairs empty with people’s belongings from 9 am, and individuals would arrive by 1 pm.

1) Capella
2) Blue Agave
3) Lemon Fish
4) Aqua Marina
5) Cielo

reviews.author: derek freeman
reviews.text:
This review is with the understanding that the hotel was at 100% capacity.

Upon check in we were taken to a “VIP” check in experience and waiting for 20 minutes to get checked in.

Bell staff was friendly and efficient
Transition and introduction never happened and was very frustrating.
Room was very nice - no room upgrade offered or was I able to pay more for a better room. No late check out approved regardless of Expedia highlighting a late check out.

Our concierge finally connected with us after going and asking the front desk how to make reservations. Mario then tried very hard to get two and was only able to get late dinner reservations due to capacity. (Would have been nice to know you must make reservation by 4pm)

In addition pool cabanas were all booked and it was very competitive to get lounge chairs together. Adults only Reserve side.

Beach was incredible and clean.

Staff we had help with during our stay.
Sante- Josue- very helpful and provided local suggestions
Gabriella - went out of her way to get anything we were looking for.
Jacob - extremely nice and worked very hard to make our pool days very fun.

Reserve bar-
Luis- ( best dirty banana in Cancun)brought the energy and made the bar vibe very fun and provided a great energy to the pool. Alejandro - was very efficient and worked perfectly with Luis.
Valeria - worked as hard as anyway that I saw and always had a smile. All three said several times they love their jobs that made our conversations more enjoyable.

Reserve coffee bar- Julio- was always friendly and did a great job managing very loud customers while still being professional to others in line.

Check in - isaac didn’t help layout how reservations worked and didn’t seem to set the team up for success.

Mario… reactive and was limited in helping due to occupancy .”possibly due to capacity” we had a short stay and it seemed like those with longer stays already had most of the reservations and there was not much room to accommodate a shorter stay.

David at the pool cabana station(reserve)- went out of his way to find a last minute reservation for us to enjoy one day at a cabana. He  also was beyond helpful and brought a great energy to the pool that lacked vibes with no music.
Victor was very helpful and their team did a great job - it was fun to learn about daisy and Venus at the pool.

Sante staff was incredible and their food was very good. Huevos rancheros and French toast were the highlights for us.

Sal steak house was our best meal with their tar tar and carrot soup being the winners of the evening. Francisco was very professional.

The buffet was incredible and very easy to access with a ton of options and seating.

Lemon fish was the worst of our experience of the trip. Two of our main entrees never came out after waiting for a 930 dinner reservation this was terrible. We left after waiting an hour for our main courses.

Agua marina restaurant was okay with both our meals having the same sauce base that didn’t show much variety. Slow due to high volume.

Wish we checked out kanna and the secluded seating.

We spent most of our time on the reserve side and the staff was all next level.

The reason we gave this 3.5-4 stars is due to the check in experience and the 5am wake up to get pool seating. Dinner reservations after 830 didn’t fit our schedule but they were our only options. Lemon fish was a massive let down allowing us to walk out of the restaurant at close to 11 with only reaching an appetizer.

Other than that we would like to go back and would look to stay longer to allow for more booking options. This was our first all inclusive and it was a good value just struggled with the competition to book literally anything.

reviews.author: Laura Kehoe
reviews.text:
We had an amazing stay at Paradisus Cancun. We stayed for 9 nights in the Reserve, which we definitely recommend as there were several exclusive activities included.

Firstly. the staff are all lovely, friendly, genuine people who really elevated the quality of the stay (especially Lalo, our concierge who gave us great advice and service during our stay, Julio from the lounge, David and Victor at the pool, Daniel at Lemon Fish, and Gabriela at Santé).

The sea views from the hotel are spectacular! We never got bored of looking at the blue gradient.

Our stay was during the first two weeks of February. I was worried because the forecast looked like a bit of rain and cloudy, but we got about 5 seconds (yes, seconds) of light rain (this was on our day trip to chichen itza, so I don’t even know if it rained on the coast!). We had lovely 25-30°C every day, some clouds but very pleasant, and clouds added to the sunset scenes! Perfect weather! But quite windy!!

The food was mostly lovely, though I Capello could improve the food quality a bit. Everywhere else was great, especially Santé and Lemon Fish.

When you’re booking, don’t forget to count the tips into the cost! Lots of tips!

Overall, brilliant hotel, and you will have a great stay if you book here.

Our time at the YHI Spa in the Paradisus Hotel, Cancun, was nothing short of extraordinary. From the moment we stepped into this serene oasis, we were greeted with warmth, professionalism, and an atmosphere of pure tranquility.

A huge thank you to Ismael, Carmen, and Evettee, who went above and beyond to create an unforgettable spa experience. Their attention to detail, expertise, and genuine care made all the difference. Ismael’s knowledge and hospitality set the tone for relaxation, while Carmen and Evettee’s skilled hands worked wonders, leaving us feeling completely rejuvenated.

The ambiance of the spa was impeccable—soothing music, calming aromas, and a luxurious setting that immediately transported us into a state of deep relaxation. Every treatment was executed flawlessly, making this one of the best spa experiences we’ve ever had.

If you’re in Cancun and staying at Paradisus, a visit to YHI Spa is an absolute must. We highly recommend treating yourself to the exceptional service provided by this outstanding team. We can’t wait to return!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 – A Perfect Spa Experience!

reviews.author: Deev P
reviews.text:
If you found my review, you just WON a jackpot, because Google is being biased and showing all positive reviews for resorts or what they call is most helpful, I wonder to whom. My low reviews and others like mine are berried/filtered out.

We just came back from this resort after staying 7 nights, and let me share you my experience as vegetarians.  If you're vegetarian, DO NOT GO HERE. GET THE HELL AWAY. Please don't take this lightly.

We had our hopes very high before booking and going to this resort based reviews that I read and we felt very good about it, but it was anything but that.

Starting with positives
- Resort and rooms are nice, but don't be fooled by it
- We had a Ocean view room and it was breath taking
- Alcoholic beverages were good. Some known brands

Negative reviews...where do I begin?
- Customer service 1/5, people were nice, but they were not accommodating, not sure if it was because of hotel's policy or what, but staff wouldn't bend
- We were there to celebrate our 25th anniversary, we requested one King bed with Ocean view upon booking, what we got was ocean view with 2 double beds. We requested to change, but we were told all sold out and we had booked 2mth in advanced
- We advised them of our anniversary date and we were told they would do something special, NOTHING...just another day
- ALL Restaurants on this Resort SUCK 1/5, Italian had to be the WORST one. As a vegetarians, Italian/Mexican food is always a go to for us, but not here. Any item that they had without meat, was HORRIBLE...horrible, the waiter at the Italian was so rude when I asked if they had pizza. He asked me is it in the menu, I said no, then he replied rudely and said then NO.  They WILL NOT / WOULD NOT do any modifications in your order.
- Nachos, OMG, horrible horrible, Chips tasted burnt all time and served by them selves, No melted Cheese.
- My wife and I got sick 3 days after getting there. We ate junk everyday. Everyday we would try different restaurants and go back to Malia (buffet)
- Buffet at Malia, OMG, who manages this? Everything is allover. if Bread is in one corner, then butter is in completely opposite corner from where bread is
- Salt / Pepper is put out in a open bowl, not in a shaker, you have to use your bare finger to pick salt, nothing on tables
- No ketchup to be found anywhere (found one place during the lunch, at Pizza place of all places)
- Pizza is prepared from ready made pizza shell
- NIGHT ENTERTAINTMENT SUCKS, It is so boring, and no, this is not our first all inclusive resort that we've been to. I would give this part 1/5
- Also everything is a UPSELL. To use any of the Cabanas on the property, $210 USD + 16% Tax / day
- Upon checking in, paid additional $30 USD for some sort of government fees

reviews.author: Debbie Block
reviews.text:
The check in was easy.  I am a RCI member and there was a separate check in. The service around the pool was great, especially Laura. We selected to use the all inclusive benefits and she knew what we wanted and thought ahead and brought us drinks, ice and other items (French fries) without asking. The pina coladas were delicious!

It was wonderful sitting around the pool and going back and forth between the beach and the pool. The chair situation around the pool was inadequate. Luckily we had people in our group that got up early enough to get chairs (530 to 6am). The weekend was especially busy. I would recommend a floaty for the pool. The whole pool is about 5 feet deep and walking on your tip toes all the time can be uncomfortable. The swim up bar was fun. It was a great way to meet people. Carlos made the best drinks.

The view out the main door walking out to the beach side is amazing. The water is all shades of beautiful blues!! The sand is great. Soft, white and not hot. The entrance into the ocean is a little tricky right in front of the resort. But, if you go down the beach a little (to the right) it is an easier entrance into the water. The waves are fun to play in.

The restaurants and buffet were good. As a gluten free person the labeling and choices were not adequate. Every meal was a challenge in communication for choices and staff understanding what gluten free was. Made things uncomfortable for everyone in our group.

We were in a 2 bedroom. One bedroom had a loud air conditioning unit. Hot tub was not usable. Old, water trickled out, and the tub was dirty. We didn't use it. The beds were very comfortable.
