reviews.author: Sonia
reviews.text:
3.5/5 Stars. This is our third time in Cancun and first stay here.

PROS: Amazing service. Cannot say enough good things about the staff. From the moment you arrive, someone welcomes you, takes you to the check-in desk. All servers from the pool area to the restaurant are super nice.

Beach is wide and a beautiful blue, sandy white beach. Waves were rough but that's not the hotels fault.

Beautiful property. The lobby is gorgeous, beautiful decor throughout.

Food was pretty good for the most part. The Al A Carte restaurants were just okay. Portion sizes were pretty small. We tried Lemon Fish, Cielo and Sante. Sante was probably the best one and it's oceanside. Buffet was good but lacked the variety from other AIs I've experienced in the past.

Pool side food service was great though.

CONS:

The hotel has too many guests and not enough chairs. I had to wake up at 6am to get chairs. After 7am, forget about getting a spot at the pool or beach. Saw many frustrated people.

The rooms are falling apart. Our shower drain was clogged and the mini fridge leaked. Staff are quick to come to the room and patch things up but the rooms are in need of repair.

Entertainment is so so. There are "shows" outside each night but they are small productions and not like the grand shows I've experienced at most AI resorts over the years.

reviews.author: Mariano SP
reviews.text:
Poor value for money.

The worst part is the quality of the food and drinks; calling it poor would be an understatement. The only halfway decent things are the beer and tequila.
Depending on your room's location, you'll have views of the sea or the garbage dump of the hotel next door... And finally, the beach belonging to the hotel barely has any sand and there are always waves, as it's the open-sea side, so the red flag has been up since the hotel was built.

The best things are the pools, the casino, and the beach club, although don't expect more than a bunch of drunk tourists, though it might be good for getting a tequila buzz...

As I said, excessively expensive for what it offers. Around $700 USD for 3 nights at the end of January, which I assume is low season.

I wouldn't stay at this hotel again. There are better options at better prices...

reviews.author: mauricio k
reviews.text:
Worst place to stay in cancun. Having come to cancun for 20 years and staying at every level of hotel, all inclusive or a la carte, and this is by far the worst experience. All restaurants, except the crappy buffet, are reservation only. Which means, you have an early dinner, look for a cool place to grab a bite at 10 that is completely empty, NOPE they can't seat you. Mind you, they close at 11. There isn't a soul inside, there is nowhere else to go because the 4 other restaurants say the same thing. You can't eat anywhere without a reservation, hard stop.  Our check in happened at 5 first day, the "concierge" closes at 5, they're the only person who can book you anywhere. So your SOL, you're literally going to go home without getting seated at a restaurant.
Room service isn't bad, takes 90 minutes at least
Bars all close at 2300. Room service can't take you drinks after 2300

Ordered drinks at the bar, they swished some tap water in the cup after someone else had used, no soap, no washing. Great way to catch something unexpected and very disappointing.

This place really is terrible
Poorly organized, poorly run. The app doesn't work
The beach isn't swimmable.
The pools aren't heated. They're un-swimmable unless you enjoy 65 degrees water
You can't eat without a reservation.
The concierge that you pay for is a joke. Only available "9-4". Waste of $$
The rooms are run down. This place is shutting down in june allegedly, and rightly so. Hopefully they don't open back up because this really is a terrible use of your money. 0/5. Awful experience
The ONLY saving grace is a handful of the staff, the majority are honestly terrible. Joan was awesome to helping us get a table, armando at the luggage check in was excellent, but the one who really saved us this trip was Gaudencio. He made the experience bearable. His counterpart Francisco en la playa was also excellent. These are the people who make the hotel and made it bearable. If you can't cancel your reservation and you're stuck at this place, find these people and tip them because they will treat you excellently

reviews.text: Great hotel 5 towers has a good location with a nice beach no seaweed lots of seating options by pool. Or beach. Room service was ok but as expected the food arrives warm or cold it's a large hotel so I understand the issue. We couldnt do any watersports due to high winds on our trip. We booked the reserve which is extra cost but was good value. They have some dated rooms but  are renovating them. Which is the chief complaint I read on reviews here. reviews.text: Joshua in guest services made our trip. It rained the entire time we were there, so everything we had planned couldn’t happen. But, Joshua went above and beyond several times to remedy the situation, and we really appreciated his demeanor, his patience, and his smile. It’s a beautiful resort and beautiful beach, I can see why the reviews are high and people really enjoyed themselves!! We just happened to pick the wrong week for weather.

reviews.author: M Lo
reviews.text:
My mom and I just got back from vacation in Cancun. We stayed at Paradisus hotel and loved most of our experience.  We loved the staff. From security, bell boy, entertainment staff concierge, waiters, Spa staff. Everyone was very kind and attentive to us! To name a few that i can recall Abraham, Victor, Gisell, Alejandra,  Valentina and wish I could remember other names, but I can't.  Everyone was great! I also loved the nightly entertainment.

The hotel looked very luxurious from the moment our van turned to their grounds when dropping us from the airport. Security has a very tight management of who goes in and out. Even keeping count of how many go in and out. That made us feel so safe.

The ambience of the hotel made me feel serene and at peace since there were so many green areas and water running like fountains. So many different spots to take pictures in.

The restaurant experience was great as well. Malva, Aqua Marine, Sante were delicious. The only one I didn't care for was Flora. They didn't have many options in the menu, unless you wanted to pay extra. We only went for 6 days so didn't have time to try the rest.

Now for the part that wasn't the greatest was our first room. We asked for a change of room and they did. The second room was so much better, but it had a leak in the wall in the bathroom.  It didn't affect us much so we didn't complain any longer being that it was a lot better than the 1st room.  I do know they will be closing the hotel for renovations this may. So hopefully it'll be much better afterwards.

To all the Staff Thank you so much! You made our trip memorable !

reviews.author: Shyna Kashi
reviews.text:
The service of this place is horrendous. The one time the hotel staff was on time with something was when they came by our room early with the luggage cart to rush us out of our rooms and get us to check out as soon as possible. Every single restaurant we had a reservation at did not seat us for at least 30 to 45 minutes after our allotted time. The staff don't pay attention to you until you wave a crisp $10 or $20 bill in the air to show them you are going to leave a hefty tip. I even once asked for some ice at around 11:30 pm one night and they did not bring it until 1am after waking me up with their knocks on the door. The front desk also never answer. Staying in their "exclusive" Reserve section of the hotel, I had called the Reserve front desk at least once or twice a day with a question and was left listening to a ringing phone for at 10 minutes before hanging up.

Not to mention the food itself is disgusting. The quality is so bad and I recommend you eat out every night. Even their "amazing steakhouse," Sal, is mediocre at best. I will admit, it was the only food I could swallow without cringing but it was nothing special. Additionally, most restaurants tend to have one or two decent menu options, but they are never included in the hotel's All Inclusive special, you have to pay another $50-100 for the edible food. The all inclusive package is useless unless you are there to take advantage of a bar.

The property is beautiful and it is such a shame that it had to be overshadowed by the terrible service and inedible food.

If you are used to the Ritz Carlton, Four Seasons, and other 5 star hotels during your travels, run far far away from this establishment. Even if you are used to Hilton and best western and other 3 or 4 star hotels, you should run away as well, this place is not the place to be.

reviews.author: Mathieu Hache
reviews.text:
During our stay at Paradisus Resort Cancun, we had the pleasure of experiencing the exceptional service provided by Abraham, Karina, Gabriella at the Ginger Bar. From the moment we approached the bar, their warm and welcoming demeanor set the tone for an unforgettable experience.

Abraham and his team demonstrated unparalleled professionalism and genuine friendliness, making every interaction a delight. They were incredibly attentive, ensuring that our drinks were prepared to perfection and tailored to our preferences. Their extensive knowledge of cocktails and beverages was impressive, and they were more than happy to recommend options that suited our tastes.

What truly stood out was their ability to create a lively yet relaxed atmosphere. Whether you were looking to enjoy a quiet drink or engage in friendly conversation, Abraham and his coworkers effortlessly accommodated everyone’s mood. Their contagious energy and passion for their craft made the Ginger Bar a highlight of our trip.

We were consistently impressed by their efficiency, even during busy moments, and their commitment to ensuring every guest felt valued. If you’re visiting Paradisus Resort Cancun, be sure to stop by the Ginger Bar to experience Abraham’s excellent service. It’s rare to find such a combination of skill, warmth, and hospitality.

The Hache familly.

reviews.author: Ryan Garcia
reviews.text:
Let me start by saying that we got a great deal at this hotel due to my sister-in-law's previous employment with this hotel chain. We also chose to visit during the slowest part of the year to get the best deal possible. However, because we used a coupon code and visited during the off-season, the hotel seemed to believe it had the right to treat my family and me as if we were not paying customers.

While the service outside of the front desk and upper management was great, and the hotel is located in a beautiful spot right on the water, the experience was blemished by an issue. My 3-year-old son and I both got food poisoning. Since this is an all-inclusive resort, everything you eat and drink is included. Unfortunately, this led to a very unpleasant stay, not just because of the food poisoning, but also because of the front desk and upper management’s refusal to accept any responsibility.

Conveniently for the hotel, there is a doctor on-site who is contracted, meaning that if something goes wrong (like food poisoning), they refuse to cover any expenses related to the doctor’s services. They essentially absolve themselves of any fault, using the excuse that my son and I could of gotten food poisoning from eating something that wasn't from the hotel. Again, it is an all inclusive hotel. I got sick on the third day and my son on the fourth day. To make matters worse, they falsely accused me of requesting free massages, daily discounts, and a free stay - claims that were entirely untrue. Never once did my group request anything besides them covering the medical bills. This speaks a lot to the character of your business and the way you teach your employees. Specifically, a front desk rep by the name of Ishmael claimed I requested these accommodations.

While parts of the trip were enjoyable, I hope that you don’t get food poisoning. If you do, you’ll be told to kick rocks, because your money was already collected. Be cautious when considering a stay here.

reviews.author: Lina Mokhtari
reviews.text:
We stayed at this resort at the end of October and the beginning of November, and even though this review is a bit late, I can’t stop thinking about how great it was! The resort itself was amazing, but honestly, what made it super special was the staff. They were so friendly and really made it a place we want to come back to.

The food was incredible! Lemon Fish was really good (special thanks to Jesus!), but Agua Marina completely blew us away. It wasn’t just the best resort food I’ve had—it’s up there with the best food I’ve ever eaten in my life! Every meal was delicious, and the flavors were just insane.

What made it even better was the team at Agua Marina. Martin and his crew were so awesome—super nice, helpful, and professional. I also want to give a huge thank-you to Erick, Sergio, and Wilbert for being so kind and attentive. They really went above and beyond, and we appreciated it so much.

We’re 100% coming back! The resort was great, but the people, the service and the food made it unforgettable. Can't wait to visit again!

reviews.text: Don’t come to this resort if you’re planning to be relaxed and enjoy your vacation. Everything here comes with some issues, and nothing is smoothly done. For instance, the pool cabanas are only given to you for free for 2 days and after that you have to pay for it. The cabanas on the beach are 250+ dollars for one day. They have completely misunderstood the concept of “all inclusive”. It’s a literal scam. Another issue is how outdated the resort is, it needs massive repair and renovations. The walls are leaking, doors are falling apart and bathrooms are never cleaned consistently. Me and my husband came to Cancun last year and stayed at “live aqua” and it was the best experience ever and therefore, we decided to come back to Cancun and since this time we were traveling with family, we decided to stay at paradisus. Overall, very inconsistent, rude service and overall unpleasant experience for us.

We recently spent an incredible week at this all-inclusive resort, and the service truly exceeded all expectations. While the entire staff was consistently professional and attentive, three individuals stood out, taking the experience to a whole new level.

Francisco, with his impeccable professionalism and warm demeanor, made every day at the beach a treat. Whether it was setting up our sunbeds or bringing over a perfectly packed beach basket with everything we needed, he did it all with a smile that instantly brightened our day.

Alejandro, always cheerful and radiating positivity, made every coffee break a joy. Whether it was a cappuccino, a refreshing iced drink, or a decadent slice of cake, he ensured we were well taken care of at any hour. His constant smile and energy were contagious.

Moses, from the Cielo restaurant, gave us an unforgettable dining experience with his expertise in Yucatan specialties. The flavors were exquisite, and his knowledge and passion for the cuisine elevated our meal into something truly memorable.

The overall service at this resort was outstanding, but Francisco, Alejandro, and Moses are in a league of their own. Their dedication and genuine hospitality made this vacation one to cherish. I highly recommend this resort for anyone seeking exceptional service and unforgettable experiences.

We had an amazing time with Paradisus Cancun. The very next day of our vacation my wife and I said the same words " we are coming back here". Great experience with our 3 year old and friends. Staff is great. I'll start with manager of Malva - Edier, what a guy, greeted every one with love and care, shows you how much respect their work and your time. There was a slight inconvenience which I won't be mentioning here and it was an unintentional one, but Edier took the service to next level and compensated with his personal attention and time and also some other non monetary (complimentary resort service) compensation which I will not mention. Till his last day he messaged me on my phone post working hours to ask me if I needed anything as I was leaving that day. Thank you Edier from myself and my family. Second name - Romeo, the property/hospitality manager. There was some technical issues with room which I addressed to a few few people and said it was being worked on and it caused a major inconvenience to us. Post 24 hours I went to service desk and Rommel was there whom I addressed the issue to and he made sure not only I that I get a better room but also complemented for the inconvenience (again non monitory as it was an resort service). Great guy with care for his job and his tourists. Never said I am busy or asked me to go to someone else. Listened to me carefully and took appropriate actions. Thank you very much Rommel, I hope I get to see you again.
Regarding resort- it's an amazing place. You will not want to step out,  I did not wanted to come back. Staff greets you with a smile Everytime they bump into you. Room service is quick and 24 hrs. Beach is accessible within 20 steps from the door of resort, pools and family area are great too. My family was safe and enjoyed a lot. Clean -9/10, food 8/10, service 8/10.
Constrictive feedback - kids area was missing. My kid was bored for sometime as there were no water slides or entertainment for them.
Post 11 there is no bar open so no night life for young couples.
Pool area needs some more accommodations as lounge seats are limited.
Shuttles /golf carts till main gate for outside travel should be arranged.
Having said all this, I am for sure going here again for my next all inclusive. Mr.Edier and Mr.Rommel thank you again for everything.

reviews.author: Khodadad Javaheri
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Cancun was unfortunately far below what we expected from a five-star all-inclusive hotel. While there were some positives, significant issues greatly impacted our experience.

Positives:
•	Beautiful beach: The beachfront was stunning and well-maintained.
•	Large, clean pool: The pool area was enjoyable and offered a relaxing atmosphere.
•	Friendly and helpful staff: The servers and bartenders were particularly kind and attentive, enhancing the dining and bar experience.

Negatives:
1.	Maintenance Issues:
•	We experienced a ceiling leak in our bathroom that required multiple follow-ups to address.
•	When we requested a resolution, we were told we could upgrade to a renovated oceanfront room for $100 extra instead of having the problem fixed promptly. This approach felt opportunistic and inappropriate given the circumstances.
2.	Cleanliness Problems:
•	We saw small roaches 3 times: once in the restaurant on the ground, once in our hotel room on the ground, and once in the hotel room drawer where clothes were stored.
•	We also found a dying bug inside the fridge in our room, which was highly unpleasant and concerning.
•	These cleanliness issues are unacceptable for a five-star property.
3.	Outdated Rooms:
•	The rooms felt old and in need of renovation. This detracted from the overall experience.
4.	Food Quality:
•	Across all restaurants, the food was bland and uninspiring, not meeting the standards expected at this price point.
5.	Missed Room Cleaning:
•	Room cleaning was missed entirely on one day of our stay.
6.	Weak Entertainment Options:
•	The entertainment was underwhelming, with short and unengaging events. Many evenings, we found ourselves unsure of how to spend our time due to a lack of compelling activities.

Overall, while the beach, pool, and staff were lovely, these positives could not outweigh the significant shortcomings in maintenance, cleanliness, and food quality. The experience was well below five-star standards, and we would not consider returning.

Regarding the facilities, it's good news to know that the hotel is undergoing renovations, as the rooms, especially, are in need of renovation due to their current condition.

In terms of food, our experience was mixed: the Santé restaurant offers excellent cuisine (even better than Sal for dinner), but the overall buffet left much to be desired. The Lemon Fish restaurant, on the other hand, was simply average and has room for improvement.

In short, the attention of The Reserve's staff is what stands out the most and elevates the experience, although there are areas for improvement in the facilities and the quality of the buffet.

We had an absolutely worry-free and wonderful week at Paradisus Cancun. The check-in process was quick and seamless. Rafael, the concierge desk representative, was very helpful and professional.

The room, while not extravagant, was pleasant and comfortable, with a well-functioning AC. The ocean view from the balcony was simply breathtaking.

The beach is a solid 10/10, with the ocean displaying every shade of blue and the water warmer than the air. We were able to collect some beautiful seashells, just needed swim goggles to pull them out of water. The waves were big on some days, but it wasn’t a problem, lots of fun activities in the spacious pools.

Malva, the buffet restaurant, had convenient hours and a wide selection of food. It was well-staffed, and the service was attentive, with Pasqual offering excellent assistance. We never had to wait for anything.

The resort's restaurants all had a lovely Caribbean atmosphere, and the food was good overall. Our favorite was Agua Marina.

The Nespresso café offered great coffee and tea options, with Alejandro and Ricardo providing exceptional service.

We definitely will return and recommend to friends.

reviews.author: Brian Reyes
reviews.text: I recently had the pleasure of experiencing hydrotherapy at Paradisus Cancun, and I must say, it was a truly rejuvenating experience, thanks in large part to the exceptional service provided by Ismael and Rogelio. Both were incredibly professional, attentive, and knowledgeable, ensuring that every step of the hydrotherapy session was both relaxing and effective. Ismael explained the different stages of the therapy with great clarity, making sure I was comfortable throughout the process, while Rogelio added a personal touch with his warm and friendly demeanor. Their expertise made a noticeable difference in the overall experience, and I left feeling completely refreshed and revitalized. I highly recommend their services to anyone visiting Paradisus Cancun!

reviews.author: ST
reviews.text: By far the worst "all inclusive" resort I've ever been to. WAY too few beach and pool chairs, to the point where we had to spend minimum 30 minutes hunting for chairs every day. The food is pretty bad, and I also got food poisoning (don't eat the fish if you do go here). Lots of upcharges for basics at a supposedly "all inclusive" hotel (better meals at the restaurants, better drinks at the bars, room service, etcetera). Tons of salespeople constantly trying to sell everyone crap all over the property. The bed in our room was very uncomfortable and made it hard to sleep well (and worth mentioning for reference, I normally sleep particularly well). To give them credit where it's due, the service at the beach and pool bars was good, most of the staff is very friendly, and the beach is very nice.

reviews.text:
This is our 4th time here and it is by far the best resort we’ve ever been to ( we’ve been traveling for 40 years around the world).
The resort has one of the best layouts of any Caribbean resort out there with the buildings, restaurants and pool within 300 feet of the ocean.
The food has never disappointed us with 8 or 9 restaurants to choose from and the service is second to none!!!
A few employees that I must point out are Laura who has been a pool side waitress here forever! She is by far the friendliest and most efficient person on the resort. Drinks are always made to our liking ( never too strong or weak) and she always seems to know when we’re ready for another as well as keeping our ice bucket full of bottled water.
Another employee that must be mentioned is Joshway the main pool concierge.
From towels to finding you a chair when they are all taken .. he’s your go to guy.
The amazing thing is that they have remembered us from past trips and make you feel like family!!
They make the stay memorable!

reviews.author: Aw B
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at Paradisus Cancun, and I must say it was a very disappointing experience. This resort markets itself as a luxury all-inclusive, but in reality, it operates more like a money-grab operation.
•	Not a Proper All-Inclusive: Most of the premium food options in restaurants come with an extra charge. Only basic food is included in the package, and even something as simple as fries will cost you extra.
•	Pool & Cabanas: The pool chairs are never available unless you reserve them before 7:00 AM. If you want a cabana, be prepared to pay a ridiculous $250 USD per day.
•	Unprofessional Staff: The staff is very unprofessional and, in some cases, outright arrogant. They are often misleading, and it’s difficult to get a straight answer.
•	Dirty Towels & Sales Pitch: Towels are handed out by the Aqua Activities team, and you’ll be subjected to their sales pitch before getting one. Even then, the towels are not always clean.
•	Constant Sales Pitches: One of the most annoying aspects was the constant interruption by photographers trying to sell their services, multiple times a day, whether you’re at the pool or on the beach.

The facility itself is poorly maintained. There was no hot water for over 24 hours during my stay, and the staff offered no assistance or apology. It also rained, and my room flooded. This wasn’t an isolated incident — multiple families experienced the same issue. The staff showed no urgency in helping us.

The food quality was average at best, and several people in my group experienced vomiting and diarrhea. To make things worse, the chefs hardly understand English, so requesting anything customized is pointless.

Overall, this resort fails to deliver a true all-inclusive luxury experience. It’s overpriced, poorly managed, and focused on upselling services instead of guest satisfaction. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone looking for a relaxing and hassle-free vacation.

Dear Guest Service Center Management,

Thank you for your response, but I must express my disappointment with the dismissive tone and lack of accountability in your reply.

Firstly, referring to your offerings as "an array of gourmet options included in your stay" is misleading when basic items like fries and guacamole are either unavailable or come at an additional cost. This is not the hallmark of a true all-inclusive luxury experience.

Secondly, the suggestion to make early reservations for cabanas disregards the fact that a $250 USD daily fee is far from reasonable for most guests. Calling it "an inviting and relaxed atmosphere" does not justify the exorbitant cost.

The unprofessional attitude and lack of urgency shown by your staff during serious issues, such as room flooding and the absence of hot water for over 24 hours, are unacceptable. Your team’s failure to address these matters adequately left many guests feeling neglected.

Additionally, your claim of prioritizing cleanliness contradicts my experience. Towels were not only unclean but were distributed after an intrusive sales pitch. Furthermore, the pool cleanliness left much to be desired, with sand present and the water being too cold for comfort.

As for the culinary experience, describing it as “inspiring and delicious offerings” is disingenuous when the food quality was subpar, and several guests in my group fell ill. The language barrier with your chefs compounded the issue, making it impossible to request customized meals.

Your response has only reinforced my perception that guest satisfaction is not your priority. I hope you take this feedback seriously and implement the necessary changes to meet the expectations you set through your marketing. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I cannot recommend your resort and will be sharing my review with others to help them make informed decisions.

reviews.author: Nancy Ruvalcaba
reviews.text:
The beach and food was great, the entertainment options were great, the staff was friendly. The beach was nice and clean, but waves were a bit aggressive in early December. I will say that the beach/pool lounging chair system needs to be improved. I have stayed at Paradisus Los Cabos and Paradisus Dominican Republic and they both have a system where they give you a card for a towel and you have to return the towel to get the card back. Here at Paradisus Cancun, you can get as many towels and basically reserve as many chairs at the beach and the pool at the same time. My family and I had a hard time finding beach/pool lounging chairs even though many were not being used all day because they had a towel and it was hard to tell if people were currently using them or if they had left for the day and were not coming back. Many people had to sit on the sand when there were many available chairs that were not used all day but had a towel on them. Mixed drinks on the beach taste watered down but the drinks poolside and bars were ok. I noticed there was a lot of cosmetic repairs needed around the resort and signage that needs to be implemented. If you get lost, you have to ask around but there is not much signage at this resort compared to their other 2 locations I have been to which was disappointing. The pool also did not have signage of how deep the pool was so that was tricky. Good resort, but has some kinks to work through.
I also wanted to mention that Nestor the outdoor entertainment host is a gem. He knows how to work a crowd especially during Movie Trivia.

reviews.author: George
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed for 5 nights in January 2025 at the beautiful paradisus cancun resort. Every view in the resort is breathtaking, especially the incredible decor and lively lobbies full of plants that stretch from the ceiling to the floors. The beaches are very beautiful and clean, the pools are large and a lot of seating. The rooms are very nice and accommodating with great views. There is a wide selection of food to satisfy any craving you may have, and let's not forget the wonderful drinks they will serve you all day.

The reserve section was an upgrade we chose and it is very worth it with extra amenities and included bonuses, including an adult only section and pool area.

The staff across the entire resort is what really makes this place special. Everyone is super friendly and helpful. They all went above and beyond to make sure we had what we needed. I commend ALL of the staff here, not one complaint. Ramiro Armando Manuel was the last server on our trip before we checked out and he was so nice to make sure we had a great last morning.

reviews.author: ABADÍA DE YUSTE de Rubén Hornero
reviews.text:
As a Circle Blue member, this hotel is a disappointment because they're not yet ready for it. We booked Circle Blue at the Paradisius in Punta Cana, which included all the amenities they offered, and arriving here full of excitement has been a disaster because they have nothing to benefit club members. They're simply not prepared. In Punta Cana, where we booked, there was an exclusive members' area on the beach and pool at lunch and dinner, and there was a wine list with about 20 different wines and cavas.

We went down to dinner and were told we only had one cava and two red wines, neither of which were very good.

In the beach area, it doesn't matter if you're a Circle member or not, and in the pool area, you don't have any privileges either. This has cost us 36,000 options, which is a lot of money. We've been talking to the Circle members' area, and well, they haven't really offered any solution. We even told them we'd file a complaint, and they didn't seem to care. But we'll do everything we can to make sure this doesn't end here. They've played with our money and our hard work.

**DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY!**

Our stay was a complete disaster, and I don’t even know where to begin. We booked a Family Concierge Junior Suite with an ocean view directly through the Melia website for 4 nights and 5 days, and I specifically requested a king bed. Instead, we were given a room with two double beds.

To make matters worse, our first room was filthy. All the glass doors and mirrors were smeared with dirt, there was a ball of hair on the shower floor, a used razor was left in the shower caddy, and water wouldn’t drain from the shower. The room also had a revolting smell. I immediately complained to the front desk, and they assured me someone would come to clean the room again and that we’d be moved to a room with a king bed the next day. However, after housekeeping came and went, the room was still just as dirty. The only change was that they sprayed an unbearable air freshener throughout, making the smell even worse. We had to air the room out for an hour, but it was still difficult to stay in because of the overpowering stench.

The next day, we were moved to another room, but once again, it had double beds although I was ASSURED that this time, the room does indeed have a kind bed. Although the new room was clean, the air conditioning didn’t work properly—it wouldn’t turn off, and we couldn’t adjust the temperature or fan speed. And as if that wasn’t enough, after a heavy rainfall, our room flooded, and we had to use towels to contain the water.

On top of the filthy, faulty rooms, the food was dreadful. The sushi at Lemon Fish was worse than supermarket sushi, and the food at MALVA Food Bazar was either bland or downright disgusting. The pizza from Mascalzon was tasteless, and the food ordered by the pool was stale and disappointing. Even the sodas were watered down. The vegetarian options were extremely limited and what little vegetarian food was available was always contaminated with meat due to a lack of serving utensils by each dish. The food was so bad that my kids survived on nothing but bread, fries, chips, and fruit during our entire stay.

The staff constantly expected tips for even the smallest service. If you gave them anything less than $5, they would give dirty looks and delay service for the rest of the day.

Bottom line: DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS HORRIBLE HOTEL. We deeply regret our decision, and you will too!

reviews.author: Priscilla tran
reviews.text:
I wish I could give this resort zero stars. I feel compelled to warn others about what we went through.
Rooms: The rooms were extremely outdated, poorly maintained, and downright dirty. Basic amenities like outlets stopped working halfway through our trip, leaving us frustrated and unable to charge essential devices. Despite paying for what was supposed to be a relaxing vacation, we were greeted with conditions that felt more like a budget motel than a resort.
Cockroaches: Things took an even worse turn when one of the rooms found cockroaches. Understandably, they asked to be moved to another room, only to find another cockroach in the new room. When we reported this to staff, their reaction was appalling—they were completely unapologetic and unsympathetic, acting annoyed and even sighing as if we were inconveniencing them by pointing out this serious issue. No guest should ever feel dismissed when raising such a legitimate concern.
Food Safety: As if the room issues weren’t enough, five of us ended up with food poisoning from the resort's food. This ruined several days of our trip, leaving us miserable and unable to enjoy any of the activities we had planned. The lack of hygiene and food safety is deeply concerning, and it’s clear they don’t prioritize the health or well-being of their guests.
Service: The staff, especially at the front desk, were among the worst I’ve ever encountered. They seemed indifferent to our complaints and acted like they didn’t want to be there. Anytime we tried to bring up an issue, we were met with sighs, eye rolls, and an overall attitude that made us feel unwelcome.
The lack of care and professionalism across all aspects of this resort is astounding. From the poor room conditions and pest issues to the food poisoning and unhelpful staff, it’s hard to believe this place is even operational.
Do yourself a favor and avoid this resort at all costs. Cancun has plenty of other options that will offer better value for your money, along with the basic cleanliness, safety, and service you’d expect from a resort. Don’t make the same mistake we did. This place is an absolute disaster.

reviews.author: Ashley N
reviews.text:
Wouldn't recommend this resort, here's why:

Cockroachs:
There were cockroaches in our room in building 1 by the mini fridge. So we asked to move rooms.  The staff member we talked to literally sighed on the phone at our request so they know it's an issue. He wasn't even apologetic or the least bit sympathetic to the situation. They moved us to a room in building 3, where we ended up seeing another cockroach in the bathroom.

Rooms:
Our room was outdated and didn't look like the pictures. Our shower would literally leaked water everywhere. The bed wasn't soft and had stained sheets. There were not enough outlets, and some didn't even work to begin with. Honestly, the room felt like a cheap motel, not an all-inclusive resort.

Food:
The food at the buffet was bland, dry, or cold. It gave multiple of my friends food poisoning. Room service food tasted even worse, so I wouldn't recommend it.  It always came cold and felt like a middle schooler made it.  The restaurant food was decent but you have to book a table in advance.

Lack of activities:
For an all-inclusive, there wasn't much to do at the resort. Because of the poor food and lack of activities, I consistently wanted to leave and go out to find something to do/eat. Which really defeats the point in staying at an all-inclusive to begin with.

This resort was so lack luster, save yourself the trouble of risking taking home a roach infestation and book somewhere else.

reviews.author: Vaishnavi Reddy
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at Paradisus (Pyramid 3) and unfortunately, my experience was far from satisfactory. Despite being an all-inclusive resort, the quality of the amenities and services left much to be desired.
The rooms were outdated and in dire need of renovation. There were visible damages to the infrastructure, which made the stay uncomfortable. The trash was not cleaned up when we first went in and we needed to coordinate back and forth with the hospitality front desk to get the maintenance team fix issues with the bathroom  which cuts into our time at the resort as we have to be available for the maintenance team's unscheduled visit to explain the issues. They never gave us a change of room and asked us to pay extra for an upgrade thus leaving us stuck in the same room. The bath tubs and the sink were damaged and outdated causing leakages.
The buffet food was subpar, lacking variety and flavor. It was quite disappointing considering the resort's all-inclusive promise. The staff at Malva buffet did not backfill the dishes and always had missing cutlery.
The staff's attitude was another major letdown. They were often rude and unhelpful, which significantly impacted the overall experience. Gabriela at the front desk was very unempathetic and impolite even on the day of check out when we shared about our experience at the resort.
The remaining restaurants require reservations so please expect long waiting time to get in line and most restaurants were disappointing with inadequate staff who were unable to attend us for 30 mins after getting seated.
Overall, I would not recommend Paradisus to anyone looking for a pleasant and relaxing vacation. The only plus point is the direct access to the beach with cabanas which is something I will fondly remember. There are better options available that offer superior service and facilities on the same hotel strip.

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I went to Cancun for new year’s and had a lackluster experience at Paradisus.
TLDR: not worth the price, many inconveniences, could most likely find much better service for the same price somewhere else

We’ve never done an all inclusive but wanted to go to cancun for a relaxing trip and spend our time in the resort. We stayed for 3 nights. The staff was very friendly and spoke/understood english. However, there were many inconveniences that did not make this place worth it. The most annoying thing was the power would go out in our room periodically. At first we called the front desk and they said it was a breaker issue. However, it kept going out and for some reason we would have to open our door and then close it for the lights to come back on. Not sure what the issue was but it was definitely inconvenient. Also I know it wasn’t the lights being motion censored because the power for the outlets charging my phone would stop working as well. Secondly, you have to make all dinner reservations in person. We waited in line for an hour on our first morning to make a reservation for new year’s eve dinner. Their NYE special dinner event was $90 per person and we did not think that was worth it considering the food we had thus far wasn’t great. There was no big NYE celebration for guests unless you paid for the event. It was frustrating that we wasted an hour waiting in line for this.

My boyfriend had called ahead of our stay and booked a massage and facial for us. However when we went to the spa for our appointment, they couldn’t find it and said they were booked up for the day. They were able to get us a spot for the next day but it was inconvenient since we had planned our morning/day around the spa appointment we thought we had. The spa experience itself was nice but it was quite expensive, over $300 for the both of us for the hydra therapy (which was “free”) and a 50 min massage. The massage was nice but I’ve had better in NYC for less than $100 for an hour long treatment. On our last night we ordered room service and were told it would take 40 minutes. After over an hour our food hadn’t arrived and we had to call to make sure we would still be able to get it.

We tried to make transportation accommodations to the airport but were told it was only for guest who stayed 4+ nights, otherwise it was $85 which was quite expensive considering the drive was only 30 minutes. We ended up booking a shuttle through a separate company for $45

The only good thing about this place was the pool service and private beach. However, we had to wait 30 minutes to get towels on the first day (we went out around 12 pm). I understand we went at a busy time of year and the place was likely very booked but things like that just did not make this place worth it for the price. The next day we went out at 10 am and still weren’t able to find seats around the pool or beach. And any resort in cancun would get you the same kind of pool/beach service so it wasn’t exactly special.

reviews.author: Mitch Raley

reviews.author: Brittany Sheppard
reviews.text:
The location and beach at this resort are perfect. HOWEVER,

This hotel is seriously lacking in all other areas. The rooms are nice and spacious however the showers and bathroom area need updating. The other issue with the room is the balcony. If you are sitting in the lounge chairs provided the only thing you are looking at is the concrete wall in front of you and cannot see the ocean (this is in every room).

The main issue at this resort is the service. It was absolutely horrible. We booked the Reserve so we had our own check in area however check in still took an hour.  They had my husband and I in a room with 2 double beds when my reservation had booked a king. They were "trying to see" if there was a king available but was advising that since it was a busy time there might not be. After seeing me immediately annoyed and mentioning that I booked a king suite, he was eventually able to locate one. My In-laws has the same experience checking into their room.

The service all around the entire hotel was just awful. We waited over an hour and a half at EVERY restaurant EVERYDAY to get our food and a bunch of times the food was never even bought out (specifically Lemon Fish, Aqua Marina, Sante, Blue Agave, Sal). My husband was furious after waiting over an hour for 4 tacos at Blue Agave. Waiting so long wastes a huge chunk of your day when you want to be out in the sun enjoying the beach or the pool. The buffet was not great and is poorly designed. They have egg stations however be prepared to wait over 30 minutes while being bumped by several passing people moving around buffet and children running.

The food quality overall was not great. The only place we had decent meals were at Sante and Sal (both only allowed for Reserve Side Guests) however it still took over an hour.

The Atrium is an area in the Adults Only section that serves breakfast and lunch and has a bar. There are not many people there so it does not get busy however one morning my Father In Law ordered a bagel with salmon and they advised him it would be over 45 minutes which was ridiculous.

The service around the pool and and the beach is non-existent. If you are not in the first two umbrellas on the beach in the Reserve side then no one will come to you. You are not allowed to sit in any of the pool cabanas unless you reserve them ahead of time however you are only allowed 2 per stay. The worker who does the seating is extremely inflexible so if you do not like your cabanas location, too bad (even if there are several still open).
My father in law had asked several people to send a waiter over however the only person who kept continuously coming over was someone from the property trying to sell time shares which was extremely annoying.

SIDENOTE: There is NO SWIM UP BAR in the adults only section! Which was pretty shocking to me and major thumbs down.
The daily/nightly activities and entertainment are pretty awful. (except for the New year's Eve Show)

Due to its many issues, Lalo the concierge explained that this hotel is closing in May 2025 for a year and a half to conduct renovations.

The only positive to this place was Lalo the concierge. He was able to book all of our reservations and get everything done that was requested him.  He advised us that at Sante (Reserve Guests Only) they do a special dinner on Thursdays. We did ours the night before we left and it was the ONLY time we got good service and our meals came quickly (it is a set menu).

We went for New Years Eve which they did a pretty good job on the event. The service that night was actually pretty attentive (due to it being in the ballroom and it being the catering staff).

My advice is SKIP THIS HOTEL. Although it looks beautiful you waste a lot of time and money here because a lot of things are "Extra Charge". Book somewhere else if you don't want to spend your entire vacation waiting in restaurants for mediocre food.

reviews.author: Rachel Bostron
reviews.text: My experience at Paradisus was just decent. I say this only because we paid extra for The Reserve and I have never experienced such disorganization and would expect better service since being in the Reserve is suppose to provide a higher tier experience. My "concierge" although very friendly never sent me schedules or information about most things she said she was going too. She basically booked two dinners for me which I would of rather done myself. Also the stay is suppose to include Sals steak house which was too full so I never got to have dinner there, 2 FULL bali bed days which I was waitlisted for, thank god people did not show up or else we only had a reservation for one full day which was the day we were leaving. The first night we arrived we were forced to eat at the buffet because no one told us that we needed to book dinner reservations or helped us do that, apparently concierge is suppose to reach out before your trip and set you up for that night with reservations. I also had to book my own transportation to and from the hotel which with other resorts this is not the case. The service people were always nice, but never memorable. The food was edible but most things lacked salt and flavor, absolutely not the food id would expect at a "5 star" resort the only food we really enjoyed was dinner at the specialty restaurants. It seemed this place was very short on staff alot of times there were lines with only one person working at a station. Restaurants were all "full" but yet all the seats were empty. It was odd. The rooms are a little outdated water leaked all over the floor because the shower door didnt close all the way and the air conditioner ran 24/7 and was very loud and most of the outlets near the bed did not work. Nightly and even day activities were sparse and everything is closed right before 11, so if you are a person who likes to do things an have experiences dont count on this resort to provide that. And then upon checking out concierge said they would reserve a changing room at 3pm before our picking up at 4pm. When I went to guest services to tell them about the changing room they said "Oh they are full" so whats the point of the reservation? Really none of it made sense. Although its a beautiful resort, and the cleaners are very good btw, I would not stay again and definitely would not pay extra to be a reserve guest since everything included pretty much was not.

reviews.author: M Scott Martin
reviews.text:
We booked a 7-night stay over Christmas at Paradisus Cancún, a Meliá hotel. It’s hard to describe how disappointed we were. We booked a “Premium Suite Lagoon View” room which was pricey – and we booked it more than 8 months early. What we got was a first-floor room in the timeshare section with a view of the hallway doors that lead to the pool area. It wasn’t even on the correct side of the building. The bedroom flooded when it rained, the kitchen fan made a noise so loud it couldn’t be used, and the bathroom sink drained slowly.

The reservation desk just said that room types aren’t guaranteed and that no other rooms were available. We even offered to have our room downgraded. We asked for a manager and were taken to guest services instead. They offered to give us access to the spa for a day – not spa services, just access to the spa (sauna, etc.).

This was the beginning of a very discouraging stay at Paradisus Cancun. We had the all-inclusive package but found out that in order to have dinner at any of the included restaurants, you had to book them between 10AM and 4PM, a time when most people are on excursions. And the reservation desk usually had a very long line. So, we were forced to eat our first 2 dinners at the buffet, which is mediocre at best. Their coffee was weak.

We finally were at the hotel 1 day between 10-4 & were able to make dinner reservations for the rest of the stay.  We found Sante, Aqua Marina, and Flora to be excellent restaurants.  However, the house white wine included in the price wasn’t drinkable and the red was very low-end. We had Christmas dinner at Capella, and this was worse than the buffet. The food looked like it had been warmed over from days before. Thankfully the live Christmas show that was blasting into the restaurant got rained out halfway through dinner and our group could finally talk.

The other 3 rooms booked for family members were better – the only complaint was lack of hot water. Several times it was tepid and one time it was cold.

We did enjoy the grounds, the pools and the beach and the staff was pleasant. The hotel has great potential. If you have a decent room with a view, you will likely have a better experience than we did.

One other note: for tipping, take lots of smaller bills in pesos with you as we couldn’t get change anywhere at the hotel.

reviews.author: Aj Makeup
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at a Paradisius for the second time, 1st time was in playa and this time cancun. My experience was not as pleasant as what I expected.

1st the food, the selection at the buffet was horrible, at one point I was just eating breakfast there because they couldn’t mess up egg so I was safe but the food was tasteless and always cold. Very disappointing there’s only one buffet for the family & adult side.

Now the beach restaurant & beach bar I was a major disappointment. The service was far from what I expected, they would come once every 2hrs on the beach for drinks I would always have to leave my chair and go get my own drinks annnnd still tip them at the bar.

Now the food area by the beach there are several things about the dining setup that were frustrating.

First, the resort has two separate menus—one for the POOL resto  ( burger, tacos, nachos, chicken wings…) and one for the RESTAURANT (more formal menu). While both menus come from the same kitchen, you're not allowed to order from the pool menu if you're seated at the beach restaurant. ( to order from the pool menu very important you have to have a bed or a sitting spot but you don’t because you are sitting at the beach and not by the pool). You can’t get food by the beach because the pool service guys don’t come and don’t serve you food by the beach.

Now  the beach restaurants have rules:

-You can’t order, leave and come back when the food is ready (takes about 45mins to 50mins wait to get your food)

-The insistence on dressing up for the beach restaurant is insane at one occasion, the staff told me I couldn’t sit at the BEACH RESTAURANT had to go back to my room, change into "decent" clothes( while I was already dressed up), return to order food their explanation was because theres business meetings happening (probably from the circle to sell the resort to new clients while they’re miss treating the returning ones.

-You can’t take your food to-go, you have to eat at the restaurant.

-Again you can’t order on the beach and continue to enjoy your time you have to waster about 1:30 by the restaurant because of all their rules.

-This level of formality was frustrating, especially when I was hoping to enjoy a more laid-back beach experience. Seemed like eating there was always a problem  was complicated and added an extra layer of stress. ( specifically that I couldn’t just leave to go eat at the buffet for the previous reasons listed above)

I could go on and on, on the unpleasant experience I had to go through during my stay, like room issues intense noise coming from the bathroom during the day and  in the middle of the night , or like after 23:00
there NOTHING HAPPENING on the resort its like go to your room and watch tv even at the bar I asked for a bottle of water that was in front of the lady she just had to handed to me it was 23:03 she said” ok just for this time” pretty incredible.

Overall, this experience was a major letdown, especially since it was my second time at the resort. The focus on unnecessary rules and formalities  completely took away our vacation.

Our concierge was nice and actually made a difference in our stay by booking our restaurants at night or taking care of us. So thank you Sergio!

But Paradisus never again!

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.text:
Our experience at Paradisus was deeply disappointing and fell far below expectations. Here’s a breakdown of the issues we encountered:

Rooms: The room we were assigned was unclean, outdated, and completely different from what we had booked. It did not match the photos or description provided.

Customer Service: The service was frustrating and unhelpful. When my wife lost a personal item at the restaurant, the guest services staff dismissed the issue and shifted blame onto other guests, suggesting the item might have been taken. The staff member we spoke to was unprofessional, rolling her eyes and making excuses instead of taking steps to address the situation, such as checking with their team or offering to investigate.

Lost Items: One of my wife’s shoes went missing during our stay. We checked the room thoroughly before leaving and didn’t leave anything behind. The room had been serviced the night before, so the missing shoe was puzzling. Unfortunately, based on the dismissive attitude we experienced, we doubt the staff would have been helpful even if we had reported it before leaving.

Food and Dining: The dining experience was chaotic and poorly managed. Long lines for the buffet were common, and dietary restrictions were not properly accommodated. When we tried to reserve a table, the staff made an error, refused to seat us, and handled the situation poorly. We also witnessed them giving preferential treatment to other guests who raised their voices.

Towels and Amenities: Towels were scarce, and amenities were not up to the standard of a 5-star hotel.

Overall Management: The lack of oversight and accountability from management was apparent throughout our stay. It was clear that systems to ensure cleanliness, customer service, and guest satisfaction were not in place.

This experience was far from what we expected for the price and reputation of this property. I would not recommend Paradisus to others. Management needs to address these issues urgently to meet even basic expectations.

reviews.author: Chad Suh
reviews.text:
Hotel Review: Disappointing Service That Falls Far Short of a 5-Star Standard

My recent stay at this hotel was a deeply frustrating experience that did not live up to the standards expected from a 5-star property. The service was consistently unpleasant, leaving me with little desire to return.

1. Subpar Food Quality

The food was a significant letdown. While personal preferences may vary, the international buffet became monotonous very quickly. More concerning was the poor quality of the specialty dinners. The Japanese and Italian restaurants offered dishes that were far below expectations for a property of this caliber.

2. Frustrating Dining Experiences

2.1 Lack of Availability: Despite staying for four nights, I was unable to secure a reservation for any of the restaurants. Reservations could only be made in person at the Mexican restaurant after check-in, and by the time I tried, all options were fully booked until my checkout. This rendered the "all-inclusive" promise meaningless.

2.2 Additional Charges for Dining: When I voiced my frustration, I was told that a table could be arranged if I ordered $200 USD worth of drinks. Essentially, they were asking me to pay extra for what should have been included in my stay. Reluctantly, I complied due to the lack of alternatives.

2.3 Incorrect Billing: After ordering the $200 worth of drinks, I was presented with a bill for $350. Another argument ensued, and the staff eventually admitted to an error in inputting the charges. This constant back-and-forth was both exhausting and unacceptable.

2.4 Uncommunicated Policies: On another occasion, I arrived 20 minutes late for a dinner reservation, only to be told that it had been canceled because I exceeded a 15-minute courtesy time. No one had informed me of this policy during the reservation process.

3. Poor Poolside Management

The pool area was poorly managed. Although the rules explicitly prohibited reserving sunbeds with personal items, this policy was completely ignored. Guests appeared to reserve spots with towels long before the pool officially opened, leaving no available seats even at opening time.

4. Deceptive Excursion Pricing

The excursion booking process was another source of frustration. Initially quoted at $50 per person, we were later asked to pay an additional $20 at the site. It turned out that the supposed "extra charge" was actually just a $3 tax, as indicated on the entrance band in pesos. This felt like an obvious scam designed to overcharge guests.

5. The One Saving Grace

The only positive aspect of this experience was the stunning beach. Its beauty was undeniable, but even that wasn’t enough to offset the countless frustrations during my stay.

Conclusion

This hotel falls far short of delivering the 5-star service it advertises. From lackluster food to deceptive practices and frustrating service, the experience was disappointing at every turn. I cannot recommend this property and urge potential visitors to set their expectations accordingly.

The cabanas are 200$ a DAY!

To book a restaurant? 45 min line (why have an APP for that in 2025, let’s wait in line like it’s 1989).

SERVICE HORRIBLE. They mess up and repeat themselves 200x I’m sorry but there is nothing I can do.

reviews.author: Rizwan Chaudhry
reviews.text:
Thanks GPT. So let me break it down for you:

Towels: If you're looking to dry off after a swim, forget about it. The beach towel situation is Hunger Games-level competitive. Better bring your own or embrace being a damp beach gremlin.

Buffet Lines: Speaking of survival games, there's one buffet for the entire resort, with lines so long you'd think they were serving Michelin-star meals. Spoiler alert: they’re not. By the time you get to the food, you’ll be so hungry even the mystery meat will look good.

Wait Staff: Rude would be an upgrade. These folks are auditioning for Mean Girls: Hospitality Edition. I half expected them to say, “You can’t sit with us!”

Property: Outdated charm? Sure, if “charm” includes torrential indoor rain showers. Some unlucky guests experienced their rooms transforming into Waterworld. Ours didn't flood—yay! But just to keep things interesting, the last day delivered a lovely drip-drip-drip in our room.

Wildlife: One roach made an appearance and demanded its 15 seconds of fame. I caught it on video for proof because this was starting to feel like a nature documentary: When Pests Attack.

Reservations: This is where it gets next-level scammy. Every restaurant is mysteriously "fully booked" despite glaringly obvious empty tables. But if you press them hard enough (and maybe perform an interpretive dance?), suddenly a table materializes. Magic! Or gaslighting—jury's still out.

Shower: If you love the thrill of a weak drizzle masquerading as a shower, you're in luck. The water pressure was so pitiful, I started calling it "the whisper wash."

Nightlife: If you value your eardrums or your heart rhythm, brace yourself. The nightly party bass is so intense, you'll feel it deep in your soul—and not in a good way.

Highlights: The lobby is genuinely gorgeous, but sitting in it feels like being the unpopular kid in a cafeteria with a restaurant smack in the center, flaunting its inaccessibility. The beach is stunning but operates on the same cruel seating shortage as the towels.

Best tip? Leave the resort.

reviews.author: Liping Fu
reviews.text:
My wife and I had the pleasure of spending Christmas 2024 at Paradisus Cancun, and we were thoroughly impressed by the exceptional service and warm hospitality. The staff went above and beyond to make our holiday special, always greeting us with a smile and being ready to assist with anything we needed.

A special shoutout goes to the Yoga and entertainment teams—particularly Nestor, Valentina, and Lai—who truly stood out with their energy, creativity, and dedication to making every moment enjoyable. Their activities and performances added so much to our stay and ensured we were always engaged and entertained.

One of the highlights of our trip was the resort’s 9-hole golf course. The convenience of having a course right on-site was fantastic, and we loved being able to play a few rounds in such a beautiful setting. However, while the course was enjoyable, we found the fairways and greens to be overly soft, which made it challenging to have a serious game.

Overall, Paradisus Cancun is an excellent choice for a relaxing and festive getaway. With great service, friendly staff, engaging entertainment, and a golf course to enjoy, it’s a resort we’d recommend—though golf enthusiasts seeking more competitive play might find the course conditions less than ideal. We look forward to returning in the future!

reviews.author: Frosty Jack
reviews.text:
Our room was ok (Sunset view), but to be fair we booked it at the last minute as a pivot from a hotel that’s currently getting terrible reviews, so we get what we get. The food was pretty good, better than most all-inclusives we’ve stayed at over the years. The service was excellent most of the time. The real problems showed when the hotel was full, they just aren’t equipped to handle that volume of guests. Leading up to Christmas, things were crowded, but not terribly so. Three days after Christmas, things got crazy busy and you were lucky to get any service by the pool. One pretty major annoyance is the nightclub across the street. If you’re booked on the Sunset side, expect to hear their base thumping until 4am. Clearly the hotel can’t do much about this, but it’s something to seriously consider before booking this place. All in all, it’s not a bad hotel. It’s a little dated, but you’ll see maintenance people running around daily doing paint touch ups, patching, and repairs to try and keep things looking fresh. The gym was nice, it’s not often you get well maintained and solid treadmills to jog on at a hotel.

Another point of frustration was getting the room cleaned. This seemed to be hit or miss and it varied when maid service would get to your room. My best guess is this was a symptom of the hotel being full but not staffed to accommodate.

We also didn’t have hot water for one day, but in reading some of the other reviews, we were lucky.

To add, you’ll benefit greatly by being an early riser here. Get up early to reserve a good spot by the pool or beach (5:00am), get to the buffet before 8:30am, try to reserve your evening meals the day you get there (reservation times fill up). If you wait, you’ll be stuck in long lines and you’ll never get a spot poolside. Is it irritating? Absolutely, but that’s just how the game is played at a lot of these resorts.

But, like I said before, the service was excellent! Shout out to Odon at Cielo, and Martin, Cande, and Manuel at Malva! All of the hotel staff we interacted with ranged from dutiful to friendly, and none of them were rude or impolite.

reviews.author: Manish Dhawan (Da-One)
reviews.text:
Stayed for 5 nights at Paradisus over Christmas week. Rooms were ok. Not 5 star caliber (was at Breathless Punta Cana few months ago). Water leaking from the faucet-wall area. One day of no warm water.

Property beautiful but very crowded as all restaurants in small area. Long lines daily to get into buffet. Had to stand in a long line to book dinner reservations. But got all reservations as I was in line at 9:30 for 10 am start of bookings!

Best part of stay was food. It was very good everywhere be it buffet or specialty restaurants. I had heard very good things about Lemon Fresh restaurant (Japanese Peruvian) but disappointed with sushi. Rest good. We love seafood and it was everywhere and cooked very well. Loved Aguamarina, Cielo and Capella. Cielo is authentic Mexican and best.

Would book adults only resorts next time. They have an adults only section called Reserve which was practically dead. Saw no one in their pools any time. Pool space small.  Have to get up early, 6 am if you expect to find a good spot on beach or poolside as all get taken very very early!! And folks may not even show up all day. Frustrating.

Staff very nice and always helpful. Everyone did an excellent job making you feel at home. Overall, every Mexican we met, we found them to be very nice and humble. They always appreciate if you speak in Spanish.

My two Adult kids did scuba diving from Aquaworld (they have a place from where they solicit business). This was their first time. It included 1 hour of lesson- Instructor Raphael was fantastic and an expert. Their whole experience was excellent.

reviews.author: Shoaib Iqbal
reviews.text:
I’m perplexed by all the good reviews. The property is nice looking. But it ends there. I believe they’re closing down in March for a year for a full renovation so it’s basically like a review reset for them. They don’t really have any interest in providing good service, and it shows. Absolutely horrendous service from the front desk to the waiters at the restaurant. It seems like the direction to provide mediocre or average service at best is given from the top down. They would routinely lie to our group or tell us fake wait times. Once we ordered room service- which is not good at all by all accounts- and waited 1.5 hours. Called 4x. It never came. Each time they said it was coming and eventually we were priority. It seems like everyone is in on it at the property, except the guests. I have 10 other stories that are equal or worse than this, but the review would be too long then.

MOST IMPORTANTLY: do not stay in tower 3. There is a lot of noise from a nearby club that will keep you awake. Not just noise. Bass. That you feel in your heart. From 1-4am. I asked them weeks out to not put us there, 8 rooms. I think as a result of my request they put us as close to the club as possible. In tower 3.

As for the rooms themselves- think of a motel room in the 90s in the USA. Same thing. Worst condition. My room literally flooded. A large amount of water came into my room from the balcony. Do you think the hotels not aware of this or that this is the first time that’s happened? They just let it be. Probably until March.

Please just do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.  Before March and probably after their renovation. You will thank me.

reviews.author: Allie Katz
reviews.text:
I don’t typically leave reviews, but my experience of Paradisus Cancun was NO WHERE near what I hoped or expected, especially given the cost.

By no means was everything awful. The public spaces in the resort were largely quite lovely and pleasant to be in. The resort was large and didn't feel overly crowded, though around meal times the parts of the resort where most of the restaurants were could get quite busy. The spa was small but nice and the massage therapists were fantastic. It felt like certain staff members went above and beyond and some of the food was quite tasty.

But that’s kind of where the pleasantness ends. The whole resort in a lot of ways felt like a bait and switch. We bought into the premium all-inclusive package, or The Reserve, as they call it, which supposedly included access to an adult only area in the resort, premium alcohol and food, and a private concierge. The adult only area was fine, though not particularly large, and the private concierge was helpful, but even though we were lead to believe that we would have access to everything as part of the Reserve, we would discover later that premium alcohol was only included within the sectioned off parts of the resort, and that large chunks of every restaurant were an extra charge. Not just a supplemental charge, but paying full price. This felt like a huge betrayal of the all-inclusive mentality, and the constant up selling of these extra charge items felt quite inappropriate. God help you as well if you AREN’T part of the Reserve, because then they really slap you with extra charges for everything. Bali beds by the main hotel pool cost around $225 for the day. At least we got those included in our private section of the resort.

The resort itself is quite run down and in need of renovation. We had to move rooms because our first room was full of broken things, like door handles and towel racks. Our second room was better, but still had a broken toilet seat and holes in the walls where stuff used to be. You can find things in poor condition all over the resort if you look. The rooms themselves also felt sparse and plain compared to the photos where the walls were painted and the room was smartly decorated. I’ve stayed in worse rooms, but given the cost of this place, I expected a lot better than this.

Service in the resort was a mixed bag with both extreme ends of the spectrum. Some staff were incredibly helpful and attentive and seemed to want to create a nice experience, where others were very checked out, or seemed untrained and confused. The people walking around upselling excursions or asking to come listen to a 90 minute presentation selling their 'exclusive membership' (think time share but maybe worse) were also a bit much and not what you want when you're trying to relax. I feel bad because clearly some folks are trying really hard, but on the whole their effort is not enough to make up for all the short comings of this place.

There's just a pervasive cheapness to this place that feels like it goes hand in hand with all the upselling. The lack of physical menus anywhere, QR codes that lead to broken web pages or apps that barely function, and cheap plastic cups instead of glassware everywhere but the nice restaurants. Menu items would arrive missing ingredients, if they were available at all. Corners seemed to have been cut everywhere, and it's not what you should get when you're spending as much as you are to stay here.

Tldr: this place is pretty on the surface, but it’s run down and not a true all-inclusive resort in the end, instead it’s one where only half of the offerings are actually included and you’ll get pushed towards spending more money at every turn.

reviews.author: Rebeca Oliver
reviews.text:
I cannot recall ever having to write a bad review for a hotel before. I stayed at Meliá Paradisius Cancun recently, and it was a complete disaster. The hotel was overcrowded, making it nearly impossible to enjoy anything. Worse yet, there were never any staff available to help. When I asked for assistance, I was either ignored or told there was nothing they could do.

I have severe vegan and gluten-free restrictions, and the hotel failed miserably to accommodate them. Room service repeatedly sent meals I couldn’t eat—vegan chia pudding with yogurt, and gluten-free bread that contained eggs. Staff at the restaurants didn’t know the ingredients and couldn’t be bothered to find out. They offered no solutions, leaving me frustrated and hungry.

The room itself was awful—old, poorly maintained, and without hot water for three days. One day, there wasn’t even running water. It felt like the hotel didn’t care at all.

This disaster ruined my birthday. I was forced to check out early and pay extra for another hotel, when they were about the same price to begin with. Although the hotel promised to refund my unused days, I still haven’t received my money.  I'd prefer to never deal with this chain again.

This was one of the worst travel experiences I’ve ever had. Save yourself the stress—don’t stay here.  The glowing reviews must be fake.

reviews.author: beka Babakishvili
reviews.text: We are currently staying at the Paradisus Cancun, and so far we’ve been very disappointed. Long lineups for the buffet and cafe, shortage of toppings/salsas at the taco stand near pool, every day no towels available (some guests walk away with several towels - there is no efficient system to make sure all guests are accommodated), lack of waiters (takes a long time to be served and food is left out for long periods of time in lobby/bar/recreational areas. We’ve left our room in the morning and returned late in the afternoon - our room wasn’t cleaned except for water bottle refill (they took a 10 dollar tip meant for the cleaning staff). Also clumps of hair on the exterior dining furniture. We expect a cleaner facility at this resort. Lastly, the entertainment has been underwhelming. For such a large resort - they set up a small stage and seating area. The resort and staff do not seem ready to accommodate all guests at peak season. We hope things will get better, but so far we’ve been struggling to find the positives.

reviews.author: mohit bhatia
reviews.text:
Disappointing Start to Our Stay at Paradisus Cancun

I'm writing this review after our first day at Paradisus Cancun, and unfortunately, it's been a disappointing experience so far. We arrived at the resort excited for our vacation, but the check-in process was a nightmare. The queue was incredibly long, and it took us over an hour to get checked in. This was not the welcome we were expecting.

Once we wait for our room, we were looking forward to exploring the resort and trying out the food. Unfortunately, the food was just average, and what's worse, there was no allergy information label available with food, it’s either missed or wrong label. As someone with food allergies, this was a major concern for me. It was very difficult to identify which foods were safe for me to eat, and we had to rely on the staff to provide us with information, which was not always accurate.

Overall, our first day at Paradisus Cancun has been a letdown. We're hoping that things will improve over the next few days, but for now, we're disappointed with the service and amenities.

*Rating:* 2/5 stars

*Recommendation:* If you have food allergies, be prepared to ask a lot of questions and take extra precautions. Also, consider arriving early for check-in to avoid long queues.

I hope this review helps others who may be considering staying at Paradisus Cancun.

reviews.author: Aditi Mehta
reviews.text:
We just spent a week at Paradisus Cancun Resort with my family, and it was an amazing experience from start to finish! There were so many fun activities for both kids and adults—we were never bored for a second.

As vegetarians, we were a little worried about the food options, but wow, they completely exceeded our expectations. There was always something delicious to eat, and none of us went to bed hungry even once!

The property is absolutely beautiful, and the people there are so warm and welcoming. The whole place just has such a great vibe.❤️

One of the highlights of our trip was their photoshoot facility. Photographer Denial was incredible! He captured such beautiful memories for us, and the service was quick and fantastic. If you’re planning to visit, I’d recommend booking your slot as soon as you arrive.

I 100% recommend Paradisus Cancun to anyone looking for a fun and relaxing family vacation. We’re already hoping to come back again someday. Keep up the amazing work!

reviews.author: Shanell Amazing
