reviews.author: Md Al Mamun (Mamun)
reviews.text:
First, it’s important to acknowledge that no all-inclusive resort is perfect. However, there are certain standards that must be upheld for a resort to truly be considered "all-inclusive." These include:

- High-quality food
- Top-notch hospitality
- Inclusive access to amenities without hidden charges

Unfortunately, this resort fell far short of these expectations.

Here are the main issues we encountered:

1. Food Quality: The food was either too bland or of subpar quality.
2. Reservation Hassles: Getting a reservation at restaurants was a nightmare. Even with effort, you’d often miss out on decent dining slots.
3. Poor Hospitality: The staff seemed more focused on upselling and making money than ensuring guests had a pleasant experience.
4. Late Reservations Penalty: Arrive 15 minutes late, and you’re pushed to a buffet that offers a variety of dishes with questionable quality.
5. Lack of Beach Chairs: Finding a beach chair was nearly impossible unless you were willing to pay $250 USD for an upgrade.
6. Concierge Package Disappointment: Even with the concierge package, we were offered poolside beds instead of beachfront ones, which defeated the purpose.

It felt like the entire system was designed to extract as much money as possible rather than providing a genuinely enjoyable experience. Everywhere you turned, there was another upsell or disappointment.

That said, the beach itself was breathtaking. The water's color and the sand were the highlights of our stay. Additionally, a few staff members, such as Messro Atilano and Ayudonte Xochilt, went above and beyond to improve the experience, but they were exceptions rather than the rule.

Overall, while the beach was stunning, the rest of the experience was deeply disappointing. I’ve visited many other all-inclusive resorts, and this was by far the worst.

reviews.author: Anas Alghbari
reviews.text:
Our stay at this resort was a huge disappointment, and it should be rated as a 3-star hotel at best, not the “premium” destination it claims to be.

Upon arrival, we were told to wait hours to check in. Despite having a scheduled 3 pm check-in time, we didn’t get our room until 11 pm. The excuse was that rooms needed cleaning, but it’s hard to believe a resort of this size has no rooms ready for guests, especially when check-in is a standard time. The entire process was disorganized and unprofessional.

The room itself was filthy and outdated. The furniture was worn out and broken, and the bathroom was barely functional. The sink batley has any water let alone hot water, and the showerhead was on the verge of falling off. To make matters worse, we found ants inside the room, which added to the already unpleasant environment. Cleanliness was a major issue throughout the resort, and it was hard to relax knowing the place was so neglected.

The staff had an attitude, and the customer service was non-existent. After my wife wrote a review, we were promised by management that they would “make things right,” but when we spoke to customer relations, no action was taken. They offered empty reassurances but didn’t follow through on any solutions.

Expect to waste an hour every day just to make dinner reservations. Even when we were first in line on one day, we were denied our preferred restaurant because others had already booked. Only when we asked did they explain that reservations could be made for multiple days in advance—something they should’ve communicated clearly. The food was bland, and the main buffet restaurant, Malva, was dirty, with long lines to get in. The overall dining experience was disappointing, and the options were limited.

Despite being an “all-inclusive” resort, basic services were sorely lacking. No beach services were offered, not even something as simple as access to cold and clean water. There were no lifeguards at the pool or beach, and finding a sunbed was nearly impossible. When we asked, we were told to rent a cabana for $250 a day or just put our towel on the ground.

We traveled with a newborn and requested a kettle to prepare bottles. Instead, they brought us dirty water in a thermos, which was completely unacceptable.

Overall, this resort is outdated, poorly managed, and provides subpar service. It doesn’t live up to its claims and definitely isn’t worth the price. Save your money and book elsewhere.

reviews.author: Nilay Yuce
reviews.text:
Where do I begin? We booked with high hopes and an even higher bill, expecting 5-star luxury. Instead, we got a moldy, chaotic mess that might’ve been funny if we weren’t paying for it.

The Room: A Moldy Disco Party
We paid extra for an "ocean view exclusive room," but what we got was loud music from the activity site below every morning and blaring in-house entertainment every night. The “ocean view” was barely visible behind palm trees, and the room smelled like mold. I half-expected mushrooms to start growing in the corner.

The Food: A Culinary Disaster
1. Reservations – Chaos with a Side of Queue: Want a restaurant reservation? Prepare to stand in line for hours—no online booking, just a sweaty, frustrating mess. We tried five restaurants, and each one was worse than the last. We eventually gave up and settled for the chaotic walk-in buffet.

2. Dietary Restrictions – A Danger Zone: Allergies, religious restrictions, or dietary preferences? Forget it.

Tacos cooked with beef, chicken, and pork on the same grill, zero separation. Cross-contamination was standard.
No clear ingredient labels, making meals a gamble. If you’re vegan, pescatarian, or have a nut allergy, good luck.
I ordered Chilean Basa with risotto and got mystery fish with wheat pretending to be risotto.
3. Quality – When Basic Goes Bad: Pizza? Naan bread with rubbery cheese. Burgers? Cardboard. Chicken wings? Swimming in syrupy sauce. Even my pizza-loving kid couldn’t eat it—twice! Tacos, in Mexico, were a disaster, and even the salad bar felt depressing.

4. Walk-In Buffet – The Hunger Games: The single buffet for 5,000+ guests meant a 20-minute wait for a table, crowded chaos, and food labels hidden behind dishes. Guessing what you were eating was part of the experience—and whether it would kill you was the real gamble.

Entertainment: A Masterclass in Boredom
We expected endless family activities but got poorly planned, single-option events that started late (if at all). Rainy days were especially bleak, with no indoor options for adults. We sat in our damp room wondering why we came.

Night shows? Imagine cramming 5,000 guests into a 30-seat area for a 1-hour snoozefest. If you didn’t stand in the crowd, your only option was sitting outside in the dark, waiting for the noise to end.

Pool & Beach: A Game of Musical Chairs
Unless you woke up at 7 AM, pool chairs were impossible to find. The pool was dirty—my son refused to swim after spotting floating debris. Thankfully, the public beach nearby was pristine, peaceful, and free.

Staff: Trying but Overwhelmed
The staff was kind but clearly understaffed and drowning in requests. They couldn’t keep up with the chaos.

Final Thoughts:
This place doesn’t deserve 5 stars or its insane prices. It’s a logistical nightmare with bad food, poor entertainment, and zero consideration for dietary needs. If you love long lines, loud music, and disappointing food, you’ll love it here. For everyone else: save your money, sanity, and stomach. Never again.

reviews.text:
The food is awful—bland, tasteless, and not fit for a 5-star resort. The customer service was beyond terrible. Upon check-in, they told us they gave our rooms away and separated mine and my parents’ rooms despite booking side-by-side with sea views. With a newborn in tow, they said there were no available rooms and made us wait two hours, only to give us a terrible, outdated room.

The room was so old, the bed frames were ripped, the drawers didn’t even open, and the floors were filthy. The shower head was shaking when turned on, feeling like it was about to break. Absolutely horrific. I can’t believe this place is considered a 5-star resort—it’s more like 0 stars.

To top it off, the next day, our other family had a leak in their bathroom from the room above, causing it to flood. My aunt fell and hurt her leg. The hotel just wanted to "fix" the issue but didn’t offer to relocate .

I also requested a kettle to boil water for my newborn, and they said they don’t have one. When I asked for hot water instead, they brought me water that smelled like coffee, making it impossible to use for my baby.

I honestly have no idea how I’m going to spend the next 5 days here. This place has been nothing but stress and disappointment. Don’t waste your time or money here. Terrible management all around. Don’t waste your time or money here.

reviews.text:
My wife and I had a very relaxing and lovely experience staying at Paradisus Cancun. We really relaxed and unpacked a lot of stress from our work. This resort has lush greenery inside with water ponds and aromas that make you feel you are in paradise. We loved the renovated Grand Ocean View room, and were happy that this resort catered to a more relaxing experience instead of the loud, party resorts in the Hotel Zone. The food was also above average and we had great meals from each restaurant. We are also cooks at home and so we had high expectations which were met. We also booked this resort after watching the Youtuber "Coolist" do a review which he gave it a top, honest review.

This was also the best service we have also ever received from an all inclusive resort in Cancun. A special thank you to:
-Renan at Aquamarine. He was amazing, kind, fast, made a custom order for us, and super attentive.
-Arcie at Lemon Fish, was friendly, chatted with my wife and I, and helpful with the sushi recommendations.
-Moises at Ciallo, made us feel like family eating dinner at his house. He was super attentive and we enjoyed talking with him.
-Guys at Cappella, made my birthday dinner so special and memorable, and him singing happy birthday and giving me two tequila shots made it memorable.
-Fernando at Blue Agave Restaurant was so much fun. He recommended his choice of tacos and created a party mood for my wife and I. The two tequila shots he gave us definitely had us buzzing and smiling.
-Shera, our concierge, was so sweet and talked to us each day, making us feel valued and welcomed. She was always helpful in arranging our dinner reservations and also made recommendations for us about the cabana rentals and spa.
-Irina who served us drinks and food was a pleasure and she always asked us if we wanted any more food or beverage.
-Roberto in Malva buffet was always kind and attentive and looked after our table on several mornings. He provided us poolside service in the afternoons and thanked us for visiting  Paradisus Cancun on our final morning.

Tips and tricks:
-Burger and fries, which are the best I've eaten at an all inclusive resort, are available poolside, but must be ordered from the servers who are walking around. There is no order counter. The same goes with the nachos and chicken strips.
-The pool near the Reserve section is actually split into two parts, and the upper part closest to the rear main entrance is for all guests and is heated for cooler days. We didn't realize it for the first few days into our vacation.
-AquaMarina food is amazing and by the pool / beach. You can sit with beach clothes on and highly recommend for a couple visits for lunch and dinner
-During breakfast you can be seated at Cappella and Flora restaurant sections (even though these are separate restaurants only open for dinner).
-Ask for mimosas for breakfast in the Malva Buffet which are a treat

Good to Know:
-Restaurant menus feature prices because that's for the guests who booked the non - inclusive package. Everything is provided for all inclusive guests (except for Sal which is extra charge and Sante restaurants which is for Reserve guests). This may not be obvious at first, so the resort should put on the menus that the prices are for non-inclusive guests only.
-The extra crispy bacon in the morning was delightful and popular. If there is none, wait 5 minutes as a new batch should will be added.
-There is no coffee in the room, but the Nespresso coffee shop is open 24 hours a day. The servers also pour coffee at the breakfast buffet when asked.
-There is no "Four Horsemen" alcohol dispensers in the rooms like most family resorts, but there's a mini bar stocked daily and plenty of drink bars and artisan style drinks available
- Resort feels like an adult's only experience, but it's family oriented. Just be aware there can be teenagers and some horseplay in the pool.  You can book the Reserve area which has its own adult pool, but we found quiet places in the south side of the pool each day.

reviews.text:
Had a nice time but please believe the bad reviews too. For families and people who want to relax — December 2024 with 2 adults, 3 kids. Slept in Pyramid 3, we purchased the all-inclusive for 7 days.

1.) HOTEL- Visually beautiful and well maintained 2.) ROOM- First day the fridge was not working, we requested it to be fix, never fixed. Water leaking on the washroom floor. The closet door broke, and we had to call to fix it. We had 2 cockroaches in the room, killing only 1 — YES, very noisy can hear everything. People talking while walking by, the night music from the entertainment, fireworks and our room was by the fountain (loud fountain). We requested no Pyramid Three but still gave us Pyramid Three 3.) FOOD- Service is top notch, so please tip. Food decent but something is missing, lacking taste. Other places in Mexico have better. Favourite spot was Aqua Marina — you eat there at lunch, it opens  at 1:15PM, no reservation. Dinner, you need a reservation, dinner team thank you so much, they are fantastic! Reservations for dinner restaurants begins at 10AM. YES, there will be a wait line. We highly recommend booking all dinners. Dinner restaurants don’t show kids menus but they have a menu, ask the server for the options 4.) POOLS- Large, beautiful and can be deep for non-swimmers or short individuals. Deep areas are about 5’5 feet and edges can be 4’feet. There is a kids area, no slides, just a rectangle pool area, about 2’feet and 1 kids circle pool for toddlers. Servers at the pools, so kind and caring. They always come to see if you need anything (drinks and food). Thank you for your hard work, it really shows! Be very careful of Pizza by the pool. We ate a lot of it. Near the end of lunch-service there was no one at the station. A bunch of birds were eating the ingredients and sitting on the counter top, where they literally made the pizza. Birds were comfortable doing that, so it is probably the birds routine. Try to eat pizza at the beginning of lunch service 5.) POOL SEATS/TOWELS- There is no towel card system. You will see towels everywhere. We learned the hard way. You have to wake up at 6AM to put your towel on your spot and put a personal item (sunglasses, book, shirt, water container). First day we did not put a personal item on our spot. When we came back, someone took our spot. We asked for our spot because we woke at 6AM to put our towels on the seats but they did not move. If you have no personal item on your spot, people will assume it is available, they will move your towel off and take your spot 6.) BALI BEDS- It is $250 USD a day. If you are a CIRCLE member it is cheaper. You can get it for free, for one day if you go to the CIRCLE meeting. Which can take 2 hours of your day or if you do an upgrade— When we were there, a representative did offer $50 USD. So it depends on the person 7.) BEACH- Wonderful, very clean, the water is so blue and warm. Sand is super soft and pretty. Be careful, strong waves and not able to swim in. Shout out to the servers on the beach! You are super, I would be tired going up and down carrying many drinks and food! Especially on a hot day!!!

Visually appealing but not our best experience.

Melia Paradisus was a wonderful stay in Cancun for our family.   This has been,  hands down,  the best all-inclusive for food quality and service.  It's hard to choose a favorite restaurant, but Flora ranks up there at the top.   Our waitress,  Cynthia, did a fabulous job recommending dishes and expertly timing our food so that we weren't rushed or looking for our next selection.
The rooms are clean if not in need of a few updates (I'm looking at you TP holder and lack of plugs bedside)  but we spent most of our time around the pool, so it's hard to complain with the climate. It's a nice choice,  but needs a few improvements - online reservations for restaurants (or have more than one person making them to avoid the line), more loungers poolside, public bathrooms on every floor and plates at the coffee shop.  Overall a solid choice.

reviews.author: annischnulliable
reviews.text:
The numerous positive reviews here largely come from guests who were asked by the staff to leave a good rating. This apparently influences the staff's pay or evaluations, but unfortunately, it doesn't reflect the hotel as a whole!

The price-performance ratio is completely off (anymore). You can see that the hotel once had its heyday, but those days are over.

There aren't enough sun loungers and parasols for everyone; this has apparently been a complaint in reviews for years, and nobody seems to care. We were at the hotel before the peak season, and even then, there weren't enough parasols. It's hard to imagine what it will be like when the hotel is fully booked.

During our stay, an Indian wedding was being held; one pool area was closed for the day, and there were no alternatives other than cramming around the pool like sardines—without any sun protection, of course. Apparently, you couldn't move the parasols from one pool to another. Tough luck, or rent a Bali Bed for the absolutely ridiculous and irrational $250 USD per day. Completely overpriced and, given the circumstances, an absolute outrage!

The staff couldn't care less that there wasn't enough space or sun protection. They suggested we rent a Bali Bed, but otherwise, the only response was always, "Sorry, we have a wedding." Great for the wedding party, but disruptive for ALL the other guests!

The restaurant by the closed pool remained open; so after a "wonderful" day, we had to either shout at each other or remain silent during dinner, as the wedding was in full swing and extremely loud right next to the restaurant.

We saw a total of four rooms, all of which were substandard.

In the first room, we were greeted by a cockroach and an overwhelming smell of paint, as if the last brushstroke had been applied just five minutes earlier. Tired and exhausted from our journey, we asked for an upgrade to the Oceanside room (at an extra cost, of course) and hoped for a better one. After three days of puddles in the room, we heard a drip—it was dripping from the ceiling right next to the bed, presumably from the balcony of the room above. We also discovered that the balcony door was leaking and responsible for the puddles in the room.

We asked to be shown another room, but it also had a leaky door and water in the room. We refused and demanded a refund for the upgrade. They offered us a room on the top floor, supposedly in the highest category. There, too, the door leaked and water was in the room. Tired and annoyed by the whole situation, we agreed to the room without a refund. At least it was a bit quieter up there, and the minibar had slightly better snacks.

Every one of the four rooms had defects, from broken clothes hooks and a shower that couldn't be adjusted properly to a leaky balcony door that sometimes wouldn't open fully (this was fixed after we pointed it out). But for the prices, plus the extra cost for the "upgrade" to an ocean view room, it was simply too poor.

The facade is crumbling everywhere, and it's leaking. Both pools aren't full enough to keep the water clean when draining through the edges.

There are too few sun loungers by the sea, and some of the parasols are buried so deeply in the sand that you can't lie under them. However, Bali Beds are available for $250 USD per day.

The restaurants ranged from very good (Italian) to mediocre. The selection of vegetarian dishes definitely needs improvement!

The coffee bar is open 24/7 and very good, but unfortunately sponsored by Nespresso (Nestlé).

The service from the restaurant and pool staff was mostly good and attentive. There were a few exceptions, but that's to be expected everywhere.

Given these circumstances, we wouldn't book this hotel again.

reviews.author: John Ly
reviews.text:
This resort is extremely overrated, I was there a few days ago at the end of Nov 2024, the resort wasn't particularily busy but the service was atrocious.

CONS
1. Not enough chairs for the beach or the pool, people come and set up their towels and other items around 6 AM, you need to go before 7 AM or you won't get a seat anywhere.

2.Service was very bad, pretty much all around, they seem to be understaffed. Check in process was slow, no one walked us to our room, as we were told it was in building 4. The complex is pretty confusing when you first arrive but you do get use to it.

3. All the restaurants require reservations, even though none of them are ever full. We ended up paying for a 5 course dinner at the steak house the first night. Food was below average, even with a $70 USD bill, I was still hungry afterwards.
Steak was grissly, sides were strange (banana tartare with steak??) and the description was misleading.
The "dessert" was a brioche french toast with ice cream and creme anglaise. As a former chef, this was so digusting. They served a burger bun in the bowl as the "french toast". I get it, it's Mexico but when you advertise it as part of a 5 course meal, it's pretty infuriating.

4. Buffet food is very bad, not sure why everyone says the food is good, it's mostly pretty bad.

5. Night show has little to no seating, and the resort shuts down around 9 AM pretty much. However, you will hear noise through your doors and walls, there's no insulation.

6. No Nespresso machine in rooms, so everyone in the morning runs over to the Nespresso bar and the line up is usually very big.

7. Main pool is nice, when not busy, it's not heated though, but still nice and refreshing. Overall there's barely enough space, pretty crappy to see a family with young kids just sitting pool side, no chairs.

8. Cabanans go for $255 USD a pop, per day, they have lots of those, as they are trying to make as much money as possible.

Pros.

1. Good location
2. Super nice beach, no seaweed as it's kept quite clean
3. Pool itself is nice
That's about it, definitely avoid this place, it really sucks.

reviews.author: chiaowei yu
reviews.text:
Our experience at Paradius Cancún was far from what we expected. We paid extra for a package that included airport shuttle service, but the ordeal we went through was incredibly frustrating. Despite providing our booking information well in advance and attempting multiple follow-ups via email and phone calls (which included getting hung up on twice), we never received confirmation. Upon arrival, their shuttle company couldn’t locate our reservation and suggested we take a taxi and get reimbursed at the hotel. However, when we reached the hotel, they outright denied any reimbursement, claiming we hadn’t arranged the trip—even though we clearly had.

While the restaurant staff were pleasant, the core customer service left much to be desired. At check-in, we asked for an overview of how the hotel operates, including dining options. Shockingly, the front desk staff couldn’t provide answers. We later found out from other guests that except for the buffet, all other restaurants required reservations, which could only be made at a specific desk with unreasonably long lines every single day.

This was the worst experience I’ve ever had at an all-inclusive hotel. Guest services were not only unhelpful but downright rude. One staff member even mocked our attempts at speaking Spanish, which was both disrespectful and unprofessional.

To make matters worse, the quality of the accommodations was disappointing. Both our room and our friends’ room (who paid extra for better service) had issues. Our power went out, and our door was so poorly maintained that it let in noise all night, making it hard to sleep. The hotel itself gives off a nice impression initially, but everything feels poorly maintained, as if held together with glue.

It’s unfortunate because this hotel has potential, but the lack of upkeep.

If you’re looking for a luxurious experience with worry free services - this is not the hotel you’d want to spend your vacation at.

reviews.author: Juan Carlos Castro
reviews.text:
We were excited for a relaxing getaway the week before Thanksgiving, but unfortunately, this hotel fell short of our expectations for a 5-star experience.  While the room was a decent size, it showed signs of wear and tear with worn carpets and dated decor.  Every time we showered, a huge puddle would form by the toilet, which was a real inconvenience.  We were also surprised that the TVs weren't smart TVs, limiting our entertainment options.

The buffet was acceptable, but the à la carte restaurants were disappointing. We were especially let down by the Japanese restaurant. Despite its beautiful setting, the food was subpar (sushi rolls, ceviche, and aguachile were all pretty tasteless). We actually ended up going to the buffet afterward because we were still hungry and we did not want to get anything else from that restaurant.

Even though we visited during the low season, finding a beach chair by the pool or beach was a challenge. We often had to wait for over an hour in the late morning to find available chairs.  The "Balinenses" beds looked amazing, but the $250 USD price tag was exorbitant, especially considering it was more than the cost of our nightly stay!

We paid approximately $190 USD per person per night for a triple room, which seemed like a great deal for a 5-star all-inclusive. However, the overall experience felt more like a 3.5 or 4-star hotel with limited inclusions. To truly enjoy the resort, we would have had to pay extra for many amenities, which would likely be even more necessary during the high season.

While we enjoyed spending time together, we were ultimately disappointed with this hotel and wouldn't return. Next time, we'll explore other resorts in the area that offer better value and amenities.

reviews.text:
Overall: Paradisus Cancún has tremendous potential but has a few areas they need to improve. 1/ more staff, clearly the staff are short handed, this meant long wait times and less than ideal services in general - eg 2-3 hours at a dinner table 2/ aging facilities, the place really needs some TLC - eg during a blight of rain, you will observe leaks everywhere. Eg, a/c water trays seem to overflow, causing leaks into rooms or damaged walls and mold. You can see them constantly patching up 3/ refreshed amenities, there were a few notable things missing such as restaurants, jacuzzi and proper kids play areas to name a few.

Room: checked into a grand master suite. The first room that We received had some issues. Paint was peeling off the ceiling. It seemed like there was a water leak somewhere above the room. We had to wait the night there while they exchange the room for us. We believe that this leak had been happening for some time as there was a little bit of mold

Concierge: Sergio was great. Very prompt to answer all our questions and help us find a new room when ours didnt work out. Also helped us book various venues and amenities throughout the property. Sergio made our stay great!!

Food: Great overall selection. Great restaurants. Great service.

Pool: overall, the pool is great. Water is a little bit on the cold side. I believe one critical amenity they are missing here would be a Jacuzzi.

Poolside service; Didier Was our server. He was continually prompt. Always checked in on us. Not only offered us exceptional service, But also was proactive to get us things before we even asked for them. He got to know the family, which is great. We really appreciated him. We were a large party of 11 people, and he came to know each one of us what we wanted

reviews.author: Nathan Guenther
reviews.text:
We had high hopes for Paradisus Cancun as we were celebrating our honeymoon, but this turned out to be the worst resort we’ve ever been to. For $4,000 per person for 10 days, we expected a true luxury experience, but this resort fell far short.

Even with the “all-inclusive” package, there are hidden costs everywhere. Want a beach or poolside bed? Be prepared to pay $255 USD, which is outrageous. Breakfast after 9 am? You’ll be waiting in a 30-minute line for a table. If you want to book a reservation for a restaurant other than the buffet, have fun waiting 45 minutes just to do so.

The staff generally seemed bothered when we asked them to do their job. Our coffee maker was broken, and even after requesting a replacement, it never showed up. The mini fridge in our room was hot because it wasn’t even plugged in, and we had to call multiple times to get it restocked.

If you’re not a morning person, good luck getting a chair by the pool. You’ll end up laying on the cement. As someone with a bad back, this left me in pain all day with no way to enjoy myself. There’s absolutely no entertainment at this resort. The shows start at 8 pm but only last 45 minutes to an hour, and there is minimal seating available. If you don’t get there by 7 pm, you’ll have to stand for the whole show. After that, there’s nothing to do. The bars all close at 11 pm, so if you’re looking for a good time, this isn’t the place. This resort feels more suited for older people who don’t mind the lack of activities.

To top it off, we asked for a nice bottle of champagne to celebrate our honeymoon, but they brought us a cheap $9 bottle—hardly what you’d expect for a “luxury” resort.

This place doesn’t come close to offering the care or quality you’ll find at a RIU resort. In all my years of traveling, I’ve never wanted to go home so badly. I wouldn’t recommend Paradisus Cancun to my worst enemy. Save your money and avoid this place at all costs.

reviews.author: Chelsea Salters
reviews.text: I absolutely loved staying at Paradisus. It was a truly unforgettable experience. From the second you are on their property, every single staff member treats you with such kindness and are so helpful. Once we were checked in, we were able to leave our bags up front until our rooms were ready and change our clothes. We were greeted in the lobby with an assortment of refreshing fruit ice bars and were immediately directed to get acquainted with the property and our amazing concierge Emmanuel who was able to to make all of our accommodations from dinner reservations on and off the resort, excursions, room accommodations and more! I have never had quite an experience the wonderful experience he offered us. As soon as you enter this resort it is nothing short of breath taking. I went in September which was during their slow season but I loved the relaxing atmosphere and not having too many people around.  I would definitely recommend staying on the reserve side. We always had a cabana waiting for us and amazing food and drinks poolside. The restaurants all had amazing food but my favorite was Blue agave. The rooms were comfortable and clean. The only con if I had to choose one is that a lot of staff will stop you in the main building on the ground floor and lower level to try to get you to sign up for things like spa experiences or excursions. I personally would have preferred to not be stopped while strolling through the resort and enjoying MY time or feel like I was trying to be sold something. Although this was my preference everyone was still very kind and respectful and were not very pushy. You never passed a staff member without a smile on their face or some sort of acknowledgment. If I could give this resort 10 stars I would. I cannot wait to book another vacation here.

reviews.author: Francisco Zepeda
reviews.text:
A fairly large hotel with very good facilities. Beach access and a large pool.

The room was comfortable and had a minibar stocked with beer, soft drinks, and snacks.

There are several restaurants; reservations are required for the specialty restaurants, and the food is excellent, although some waiters are slow or inattentive, while others provide excellent service and a positive attitude.

The bars also offer excellent service and a great variety of drinks. Since I like vodka, they had Ketel One, Stolichnaya, and Absolut.

The rooms weren't mopped thoroughly; they were left dusty and didn't get a deep clean.

The main pool isn't cleaned properly and has trash. And when you walk past the restaurant, the pool smells like sewage; they should look into these things.

The breakfast buffet is very good and well-stocked.

The specialty restaurants we visited—the fish restaurant by the pool, the Italian restaurant, and the Japanese restaurant—were all very good, but the Japanese restaurant was my favorite.

For lunch, the Mexican restaurant was excellent.

Try all the options: ice cream, coffee, pizza, and wings.

We left after checkout and booked a complimentary room so we could shower and change, which was no problem.

I spent 7 days in this resort and want to share my honest opinion.

Starting off with pros:
- We got a crib for our 1.5 year old in our room on the day we arrived with no extra charge
- The staff, especially the servers are kind, enthusiastic and accommodating. The servers in the restaurant were super accommodating and made special meals for my 1.5 year old, which I appreciate so much.
- The entire resort is very clean and pretty
- There is a kids club where you can drop off your kids and they have activities to keep them entertained

Cons:
- We found out that the corn in the buffet was spoiled a couple times
- The are 2 main elevators for the 8-story building and one elevator didn’t work half the time and the other one is extremely slow
- The room is dark and outdated - the door in bathroom doesn’t close, the toilet doesn’t flush properly
- There’s leaks in the hallway ceilings here and there

Overall we had a great time but the quality of the building is not good.

reviews.author: Seyda Hetman
reviews.text:
Beautiful beach club with a great atmosphere

Review:

Although we didn't stay at the hotel, we used the beach club and were very satisfied. The process was well-organized: We checked in at reception and were then taken to the hotel beach.

For 1,500 pesos per person, which was fully credited towards food and drinks, you could enjoy the beach club. The prices for food and drinks are quite reasonable, so you can easily combine your money and make the most of it. However, additional stools would have cost over 2,000 pesos, which we didn't use.

The beach itself is clean and very pleasant, and the entire hotel complex has a luxurious and elegant feel. Even just looking at the complex was impressive – modern and stylish. It was so lovely that I wished I had more time to actually stay overnight. On my next visit to Cancún, I would definitely consider this hotel.

Overall, we were very satisfied with the beach club experience and can absolutely recommend it!

Overall this was an amazing honeymoon trip and i would come back, i believe it is getting renovated next year which will likely solve many of our issues. The room we were in is dated, most the plugs don't work, the hot tub didnt work was dirty had no plug. the mini fridge being part of the package is meant to be filled daily in our 10 day stay it was filled on arrival and one day without us calling and asking. The service around the pools is completely dependant on where you are sat, some are amazing and some seem to intentionally avoid English speaking people even with our Spanish attempts. The food well that is next level! Absolutely incredible i haven't had one bad meal! If you aren't in the adult only section cabanas are not include and are a steep $255 a day! But there is lots of space around the pool with shade. I would think maybe a system to ensure people get space. It says no reserving spaces around the pool but if you don't you are not getting a bed as lots of people do.
Most of the staff are absolutely incredible and make the experience and make jokes with you. You will be constantly spoken to, to buy extra things and experiences and become part of the melia club. This is a very steep price and out of most British people's price ranges they offered us the lowest membership of $21,000 for two years.... the benefits seem very good but at no way would you get over your money back or money back in my opinion. Honestly though it was a beautiful location and very happy we choose here for our honeymoon.

But what really stood out to me was the service. The staff went out of their way to make us feel comfortable and taken care of. They were friendly, attentive, and always ready to recommend dishes or make adjustments to suit our preferences. It made the whole experience so much more enjoyable.

If you’re planning to visit Paradisus Cancun, I highly recommend checking out their restaurants. The combination of amazing food and top-notch service made every meal unforgettable. I’d definitely go back!

reviews.text:
My husband and I visited the Paradisus in Cancun November 2024. We have been very fortunate to stay in some amazing yet very expensive hotels and resorts over the last 20 years through work promotions my husband qualified for. When we decided to do the same for our own team members, we were worried we would have to pay those prices too in order to find a nice place. We split the team into two groups and stayed back to back one week at a time. I can't say enough about the food, the location, the staff, the beach, the activities, the spa and the pools. Even the coffee was awesome. I honestly would take everyone there again next year and I know they would be thrilled.

I need to give a special shout out to Gaudencio first off or G as we call him, he worked so hard on the beach for us always making sure all our team had a drink in their hand while soaking up the sun. G you feel like family to us now. :)

Secondly, the wonderful Tanya and Carmen who work in the spa. The provided us with hot stone massages for myself and our office manager. I've never left a spa so relaxed. Your hands are magic. Thank you.

And lastly, Salvador who was our bartender at the Ginger bar. We loved visiting you every night before and after our a la carte dinners. Appreciate you so much.

We hope to see you again soon.
Your friends from New Brunswick Canada

reviews.author: Russell Whit
reviews.text: Great hotel, sad to leave our  Honeymoon destination.  We had 5th floor ocean view which was fantastic, rooms well equipped. Flora and Lemon Fish restarants the best by far. Agua Marina, great setting, pretty food but tasteless.  One criticism would be that we were overwhelmed in a bad way by the attentiveness of staff immediately on arrival and the Melia sales pitchers. British guests tend to want to be left alone unless we ask. Paradisus is an all inclusive hotel or so we thought, we found out it is a part exclusive resort where some parts of the hotel are reserved for "VIP" guests also a large number of sun beds are available for a substantial charge. Counterproductive I feel as most of these beds remained empty for duration of our stay so could have been better used by regular guests. So some regular guests were without sun beds by the pool. Saying all this, it is a beautiful hotel with a gorgeous beach and views if the Caribbean, would highly recommend. Negative comments are more if a nudge to management, the staff are superb.

reviews.author: David Blender
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed for both work and vacation.
The entire experience was problem free with lots of friend staff.
We had the opportunity to stay in the adults only “the reserve” this added to the whole experience.
The pool side and Bali beds were our favourite place to relax.  A special appreciation to Miguel out on the pool side and restaurant.  He was attentive, always remembered day to day.  Fun to talk to and joke around with. Miguel is a true top performer.  Thank you so much!
So many great people who made the trip special.
Our concierge Jose was always helpful even on his day off.
David my “ tocayo” from the pool very friendly and helpful
We met Martin one afternoon at the buffet and his stories and service were hilarious
And Oscar from our front desk at the reserve was yet just another great professional.
Thank you so much , we would love to come back and stay again and hope to see all these amazing people again

reviews.text:
Abraham's attention and shared knowledge at Bar Ginger 2 are fantastic. I highly recommend Abraham. The service from his colleagues Gabriela and Karina is also excellent.

The same cannot be said for the other bar; however, I respect their work.

AREA FOR IMPROVEMENT: The hotel's 11 pm closing time doesn't meet expectations. It conveys a sense of incomplete service and availability, as you generally expect to continue your meetings and enjoy a drink, which is cut short at 11 pm.

I must acknowledge the friendliness of the entire staff, who attend to and guide you in everything.

Thank you

reviews.text:
The hotel! The reception and restaurants are beautiful!! I think the room needs some updating—furniture, artwork, color, etc.—but the cleanliness and staff service are excellent and super attentive. They left me a hairdryer that unfortunately didn't work, and they gladly replaced it in a matter of minutes. I ordered room service, and it arrived promptly. As for the food, I would definitely rate Lemon Fish number 1, as well as Flora. A second place goes to Azul Agave, and a sixth to Capella and Agua Marina. All the waiters were super attentive, friendly, and helpful with their recommendations. We enjoyed some events: a rock band and African dance. Although they didn't last long, it was nice to break the routine. The pools were well-maintained and clean. In short, we were delighted.

Note: It's very close to Plaza de Luxe La Isla, Playa Delfines, and the museum... And right outside the hotel are trendy nightclubs. 😊

reviews.author: May
reviews.text:
I am blown away by Paradisus Cancun. Did the upgrade to The Reserve and so glad me and my friend did, better rooms and food options. The staff  is also amazing! Enrique at the Lobby helped us with our upgrade and made the process so smooth for us. Had Rosanna for concierge and was very helpful in answering all our questions. Julio at The Atrium (server) was also great, always greeted us with a smile. In the pool, David is also so kind and cheerful in getting us a Bali bed. When there is a wait for a Bali bed, he comes and finds you so that he can offer a Bali bed that becomes available. Also, encountered Diego who was so kind and helpful, he even has rescued many stray cats and took them in his home. Such wonderful people that work here. Special mention to Daisy who frequents the pool area by The Reserve 😻. She made our stay so lovely, an absolute sweetheart. I love,  love, love her so much. I hope to see her there when we come back.
Great time at the Lemon Fish. Arce was our server and was great. Love the ambiance too,  it's so relaxing. The Sante Restaurant staff was great too. Last but not least, Radda, Uriel, Nestor, and Mariel were great at keeping up with activities and entertainment. Many of the staff absolutely goes above and beyond. I'm so grateful for the many staff we had the pleasure of encountering that made our experience so magical. Only drawback is everything closes at 11pm. Also, one bartender (at night) at the Ginger Bar do not like serving the guests unless he gets a tip. Other than that, I will absolutely be back.

Blue waters, Bali beds, great staff, amazing food, no pushy timeshare scam. I could not have asked for a better vacation.

reviews.author: Brandon Halavi
reviews.text:
If I could give less than one star, I would. This venue has been a complete nightmare and has ruined what should have been a joyous time in our lives. From start to finish, Gloria and her team have been unprofessional, dishonest, and entirely unreliable. We chose this venue and paid a substantial amount because Gloria herself promised us the Del Prado ballroom. We have it all in writing and even a voice recording of her confirming this space. But when we showed up for our tasting, after flying all the way out to the hotel, they suddenly informed us that the ballroom was no longer available. There was no warning, no heads-up—just a complete shock when we arrived. They didn’t even bother to tell us beforehand.

This bait-and-switch tactic was just the beginning. They also attempted to overcharge us for the room block, quoting rates higher than what they advertised on their own website. When we questioned this, they had no real explanation, and it felt like they were simply trying to take advantage of us. It’s appalling and downright unethical.

Now, with our wedding just weeks away, they’ve stopped responding to us entirely. We are left in the dark, unsure if we even have a venue at this point. The stress this has caused is overwhelming. We had expected professionalism and care from a venue of this standing, but instead, we’re dealing with silence and unanswered calls.

To make matters even worse, they refuse to return our deposit, even though they failed to honor their commitments. Holding onto our money without delivering on the promises they made is beyond frustrating; it’s disrespectful and feels like outright theft.

I can’t urge people strongly enough to avoid this venue. Save yourself from the heartache, stress, and disappointment. The lack of transparency, bait-and-switch tactics, and appalling communication from Gloria and her team have turned what should have been a beautiful planning process into a nightmare. Please, don’t make the same mistake we did.

reviews.author: Kassandra Sobesky
reviews.text: The service was excellent! Every single staff member at Sante was fabulous! I would highly recommend the staff and the food here, breakfast lunch and dinner. Our personal concierge was Rossana and she went above and beyond for us. If I had a complaint it is that everything is shut down at 11:00 p.m. which was good most nights.

reviews.author: Tifini Aguilar
reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of staying at Paradisus Cancun, and it exceeded all my expectations! The highlight of my trip was definitely dining at Sante restaurant. The menu was a delightful blend of flavors, and each dish was crafted to perfection. The ambiance was elegant yet inviting, making every meal feel special.

A special shoutout to David, Oscar, and Gabriella at the Reserve Pool. Their attentive service and warm hospitality made our time by the pool truly memorable. They went above and beyond to ensure we had everything we needed, always with a smile and genuine enthusiasm.

Rosanna, our concierge, was exceptional. She was incredibly helpful in arranging activities and providing recommendations, ensuring our stay was seamless and enjoyable. Her personal touch made a significant difference in our experience.

Overall, Paradisus Cancun is a paradise that offers outstanding service, exquisite dining, and a beautiful atmosphere. I can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: Gonzalo. bm
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, and the service was excellent at restaurants like Sal, Lemon Fish, and Malva. However, Blue Agave left much to be desired, both in terms of service—it seemed like everyone was angry—and in the food, which lacked both essential ingredients and flavor. The hotel is not recommended for older people because there's a lot of walking and several stairs. If you're staying in "The Reserve" area, be prepared to walk a lot, as all the restaurants are centrally located. There aren't enough carts to take you around, and there aren't enough restrooms because none of the restaurants have them; they're located outside the restaurants. If you like taking photos, the hotel has plenty of places to do so, and that's about it. 5/10

He anticipated what we needed before we ever requested anything, he checked back frequently and hustled all day long. Also Raphael in the Malva buffet restaurant terrace at breakfast was friendly, remembered our morning coffee orders every day and provided excellent service. Both gentlemen are talented professionals providing some of the best service we have ever received at any resort.

Food, pools and rooms are decent but the property could use some maintenance throughout.

We normally stay further down the Riviera Maya at the Barcelo and this ocean here is stronger and the resorts are much closer.

reviews.text: i came here for a wedding and not only did our coordinator not show up to the rehearsal but showed up late to the ceremony leaving our guests waiting for 30 minutes past the excepted time. and we payed for the “elite” wrist band or package whatever, we were denied access by the workers to the stuff we should have been granted. constant bug and leakage problem in the rooms. the chairs by the pool do not recline at all and are at a very uncomfortable angle. there is also some loud music somewhere late at night, no matter the location of your room. waited 1 hour for room service. to add, at the end of the wedding the bride and groom wanted everyone to jump in the pool next to the reception, and right as we jumped in the coordinator finally did her job and yelled at us to get out. the poolside service was pretty good, special thanks to dirdir and jose who showed excellent efficiency.

reviews.author: Karla Lopez
reviews.text: The place is lovely and the rooms are quite spacious, although the air conditioning doesn't work very well and the water runs everywhere when you shower, which is why they provide a ton of towels. Despite being an all-inclusive experience, they didn't even refill the minibar water, my room didn't have an iron (although they kindly brought one), and I had to wait about 30 minutes. Furthermore, the food has a huge area for improvement. It's bland and always served cold, plus the service is incredibly slow; the restaurants close very early and they're understaffed. We waited an hour for a table, even though there were about 30 empty tables due to staff shortages, and it took an hour and a half to be served, plus the wine was cold. It's worth noting that only the buffet is open to everyone; without a reservation, you probably won't be able to eat lunch or dinner at the other restaurants. As usual, you arrive at the buffet and, plate in hand, they take all the food from the bar because they were about to close, which was quite rude since the place wasn't closed yet, and the waitress left me with the sauce spoon in my hand and took it away. Anyway, for the price, there are many other better options in the area.

reviews.author: Mike's Garage
reviews.text:
This was the worst vacation I've ever had in Mexico.
First, it was a double room, although we booked it for two with a child. They brought a folding bed for the child. When they put my daughter to sleep on this bed, she started crying. I tried to lie down on this bed and thought I was lying on a torture bed. There was mold in the bathroom. The mirror in the bathroom looked like it was 500 years old. The air conditioner was making a terrible noise. I don't even want to talk about the dust on the fan and the peeling ceilings.
On the second day, my child got food poisoning from a super cocktail near the pool. In the dining room, you couldn't find anything to drink yourself, and the tea was poured with some kind of sediment, then I saw that the teapots were peeling off and falling into the cup.
The choice of food in the buffet was poor.
The sea is opposite the hotel, complete crap. The pool is the only thing that was good in this hotel, it is big and deep, but the water is cool. The evening show was in a small room where there was no place to sit, stand, or dance.
The restaurants had good food.
A year before that I was in RIO Dunamar and everything was much better there!

reviews.author: Jimmie Estrada
reviews.text:
This hotel is absolutely gorgeous. The beach and pools are clean and nice and the service is mostly great. We had an issue with the shower and they sent someone up to fix it immediately.

My biggest complaint though was the food. The buffet was pretty bad. I’ve had better hospital food. The restaurants are very hit or miss. I really enjoyed Blue Agave but Capella was just okay and the place by the pool was probably one of the weirdest meals I’ve eaten at a restaurant. The sea bass was burnt and the mussels had some kind of Alfredo sauce drizzled on the shells.

Our room was pretty dated and the bed skirts had weird stains. One of the box springs was ripped and you could see it hanging down under the bed skirt. The bedding was not what I’d expect even for a 4 star hotel. Lumpy pillows/not plush mattress/sheets were standard threadcount.

I also had a weird interaction with a guest services staff member who misheard me when I told him my room number and then argued with me and said I gave him the wrong room number. He was not friendly and also gave me wrong information about my shuttle back to the airport and told me I’d have to pay for it and book it through one of the excursion desks in the lobby. Talked to someone else and it turns out that wasn’t true. The restaurant staff, bellhops, and housekeeping were very nice though.

I’d consider staying here again if the food was better but more than likely I’ll try somewhere else in the future.

reviews.author: Krystal Heredia
reviews.text: If I could give zero stars I would. PLEASE STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY!!!!!! I went to Mexico back in August and booked an all inclusive resort with travel to and from the hotel. Upon arriving to Mexico, we followed the instructions to be picked up by the driver. The driver was a no call and no show. We called Melia and Logitravel SEVERAL times and they called the driver SEVERAL times. They were also unable to get a hold of the driver. They told us to go ahead and take the taxi cabs and they would reimburse us once we sent the receipt in. The taxi cab was $150 USD which in itself is robbery. Today months later they are letting me know that the driver was there and they provided a blank email with a "photo" that doesn't show up of the driver being there and saying we were a NO SHOW. Our flight was on time. I have contacted them for MONTHS and today after saying I was going to write a review they said hey we apologize for the inconvenience but you were a no show. WHAAAAAT in the actual gas light scammer company is this??????? STAY FAR AWAY. Please don't go through this robbery, scamming headache.

reviews.author: Questyn Rodriguez
reviews.text:
I was celebrating the beautiful friendship I share with three wonderful people, and what better place than Paradisus Cancun? It was a spectacular experience!
The service, the facilities, the food, the activities, and the staff exceeded my expectations.
Jacobo, with his friendly nature and excellent service at the pool bar; Gabi, with her warmth at the Ginger Bar; Cielo, with her stretching classes to start the day; David, always attentive to our comfort in the pool area; Alejandro, the coffee expert; Carlos, for taking care of us during our stay… and the list goes on… so many people made our experience unique and unforgettable. THANK YOU!

reviews.author: Ana García-Allén
reviews.text:
The service at the pool with Jacobo was amazing. It couldn't be better, top-notch service and treatment. Thank you from the bottom of my heart, Jacobo, it was a true pleasure meeting you.

Cielo, incredible! What a spectacular stretching class. I enjoyed it all three days I attended. I want to come back for your class. You are a wonderful instructor, with so much knowledge of what you do, and you radiate joy and energy. Thank you, Cielo.

Alejandro at the Nespresso café, fantastic! Thank you for those wonderful coffees and for the joy you constantly exude. Your service is unbeatable.

Gaby at the Ginger bar, excellent! From the moment I met you, I just wanted to stop by and say hello and have you make me one of your cocktails. That spicy margarita was spectacular. Thank you so much. Impeccable service.

Malva Buffet - breakfast, with Enrique.

The service at Malva was very good. Enrique always showed a super positive attitude, making us feel welcome and taken care of at all times. A wonderful experience that made our stay even more special.

Thank you, Enrique. We'll be here tomorrow.

reviews.author: Lilia Marcela
reviews.text: Excellent vacation, the service was outstanding, especially Jacob at the pool and beach. He was very attentive, friendly, and willing to make our stay unforgettable. Alejandro's service at the Nespresso stand was the experience we looked forward to every morning. Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
It was our first time in Cancun, and we really enjoyed the hotel, the pool area, and the beautiful beach.
Our butler, Nohemi, was incredibly attentive and kind, guiding us every step of the way. We loved the Malva restaurant for its variety of food, and Mr. Francisco provided excellent service. Another great option was Agave Blue; the tacos were delicious, and the service was very fast. Ms. Paola was also very helpful. Ginger, one of our favorite relaxation areas, was very pleasant.
Our experience was very satisfying, and we definitely hope to return.
